source.title: Canonical representations of surface groups
source.version: arXiv:2205.15352v4, posted 23 February 2025, 62 pages, dated 25 February 2025 inside the file. Version v1 is from 30 May 2022, and the arXiv comment on v4 reads 'Updated to fix improperly rendered figure', so v4 is the published text with a corrected figure. The published article is behind the journal's paywall and was not consulted, so every locator gives the section, theorem, lemma or equation number together with the page of the arXiv v4 PDF, and the findings below are recorded against that version. No erratum or corrigendum is listed on the arXiv abstract page or in Crossref. Note that the rank bound throughout the paper is r < √(g+1), typeset with the radical over g+1; it is equivalent to the condition g > r² − 1 stated in Remark 1.8.2 and to the inequality r² − 1 < g used in the proofs of Proposition 8.2.1 and Lemma 8.5.1.

summary: Complete extraction of the 62-page paper. Landesman and Litt prove that a representation ρ : π₁(Σ_{g,n}) → GL_r(ℂ) whose conjugacy class has finite orbit under the mapping class group has finite image as soon as r < √(g+1), answering a question of Whang and giving a positive answer to a question of Kisin in the range g > r² − 1; equivalently, a semisimple flat bundle of low rank on a curve has an algebraic universal isomonodromic deformation only if its monodromy is finite. Along the way they prove the Putman–Wieland conjecture for every finite group of order less than g², and deduce that on a curve whose moduli point is generic every arithmetic ℓ-adic representation of low rank has finite image, verifying a prediction of the relative Fontaine–Mazur conjecture and producing what are, to the authors' knowledge, the first residual representations of a geometric fundamental group that are not of geometric origin. The engine is a bound on the rank of sub-local systems of R¹π°_*V for V unitary on a family of punctured curves, proved by identifying the derivative of the period map of the associated variation of mixed Hodge structure with a multiplication of global sections and then applying a parabolic-bundle estimate; the arithmetic input is the integrality of cohomologically rigid local systems, which rests on Lafforgue's work over function fields. Of the 111 items, 4 are in the pinned libraries, 11 are planned by existing layers, and 96 are missing. The routing reflects the two halves of the paper: the topological half — mapping class groups, moduli of curves, MCG-finite representations, Putman–Wieland and the assembly of the main theorem — becomes a new roadmap, since the atlas has no mapping class group anywhere, while the Hodge-theoretic half becomes a Part II of the Tau Ceti roadmap on Hodge structures, whose L3 milestone already defers variations and period domains to a successor. Three general facts about arithmetic fundamental groups go to InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.0 and IG.1, the deformation theory of §3 and the deformation-ring consequences of §9.2 to GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1 and R04.2, and the algebraicity and compactifications of M_{g,n} to AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.4, R09.5 and R09.7. Three misprints were found and are recorded under sourceIssues; none affects a proof. This is a paper inventory and routing, not a proof blueprint: the results quoted from Mochizuki, Mehta–Seshadri, Steenbrink–Zucker, Saito, Timmerscheidt, Esnault–Groechenig, Klevdal–Patrikis, Wewers, Aramayona–Souto and the authors' own earlier work are recorded as items with their own prerequisite entries and are not decomposed here.

items.name: MCG-finite representation
items.statement: Let Σ_{g,n} be an orientable surface of genus g with n punctures and x ∈ Σ_{g,n} a basepoint. The mapping class group Mod_{g,n} acts outerly on π₁(Σ_{g,n}, x) and hence on the set of conjugacy classes of representations π₁(Σ_{g,n}, x) → GL_r(ℂ). A representation ρ : π₁(Σ_{g,n}, x) → GL_r(ℂ) is MCG-finite if the conjugacy class of ρ has finite orbit under this action. Semisimple MCG-finite representations are exactly the finite Mod_{g,n}-orbits in the character variety, not in the representation variety, on which Mod_{g,n} does not act.
items.note: The central definition. The paper's slogan is that MCG-finite representations are the canonical representations of π₁(Σ_{g,n}): any representation built without naming a specific curve, or with only finite indeterminacy, is MCG-finite. Conjugacy classes of semisimple MCG-finite representations correspond to algebraic solutions of an isomonodromy differential equation, and for g = 0, n = 4, r = 2 with trivial determinant to algebraic solutions of the Painlevé VI equation.

items.name: Low-rank MCG-finite representations have finite image
items.statement: For g, n, r ≥ 0, let ρ : π₁(Σ_{g,n}) → GL_r(ℂ) be an MCG-finite representation. If r < √(g+1), then ρ has finite image.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Theorem 1.2.1, p. 3; proved in §8.7, p. 44
items.note: The main theorem. It answers a question of Junho Peter Whang and gives a positive answer to a question of Mark Kisin in the range g > r² − 1; Kisin's question has negative answers in general. Although the statement is purely group-theoretic, the proof uses non-abelian and mixed Hodge theory and, through Esnault–Groechenig and Klevdal–Patrikis, the Langlands programme over function fields. The bound is sharp for g = 1 and not sharp for g = 2, 3; it cannot be improved beyond linear in g, since there are MCG-finite representations of π₁(Σ_g) of rank 2g + 1 with infinite image. The proof is by induction on the length of the socle filtration: the base case is the semisimple Theorem 8.5.3 and the inductive step is Lemma 8.6.1.

items.name: Algebraic isomonodromic deformations of low-rank flat bundles
items.statement: Let C be a smooth projective curve of genus g and D ⊂ C a reduced effective divisor. Let (E, ∇) be a semisimple flat vector bundle on C with regular singularities along D, with rk E < √(g+1), and suppose the eigenvalues of the residue matrices of (E, ∇) have real parts in [0, 1). Then (E, ∇) has an algebraic universal isomonodromic deformation if and only if (E, ∇) has finite monodromy.
items.note: The algebro-geometric reformulation of Theorem 1.2.1, obtained from it through [CH19, Theorem A]. The condition on residue matrices is harmless: it is achieved by replacing (E, ∇) with the Deligne canonical extension of its restriction to C \ D. The paper stresses that this is the perspective the proof actually takes.

items.name: Fibral finiteness for low-rank local systems on a punctured versal family
items.statement: Let π° : C° → M be a punctured versal family of genus g curves and let V be a local system on C° of rank < √(g+1). Then for any fibre C° of π°, the local system V|_{C°} has finite monodromy.
items.note: Immediate from Theorem 1.2.1 together with Proposition 2.1.3, which says that the restriction of a representation of π₁(C°) to the fundamental group of a fibre is MCG-finite.

items.name: The asymptotic Putman–Wieland conjecture for small groups
items.statement: For g ≥ 2, n ≥ 0 and any finite group H with #H < g², the Putman–Wieland conjecture for (g, n, H) holds: for every H-cover Σ_{g'} → Σ_g branched over n points, every nonzero vector of H₁(Σ_{g'}) has infinite orbit under the stabiliser Γ of the corresponding surjection in the pure mapping class group of Σ_{g,n+1}.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Theorem 1.4.1, p. 4; proved as Corollary 7.2.4, p. 36
items.note: An asymptotic form of the Putman–Wieland conjecture [PW13, Conjecture 1.2]: the conjecture holds for a fixed H once g is large. The bound comes from the fact that #H is the sum of the squares of the degrees of the irreducible characters, so #H < g² forces every irreducible representation of H to have dimension less than g.

items.name: Putman–Wieland for isotypic components of small irreducible representations
items.statement: Let ρ be an irreducible representation of the finite group H with dim ρ < g, and let H₁(Σ_{g'})_ρ be the ρ-isotypic component of H₁(Σ_{g'}). Then no nonzero vector of H₁(Σ_{g'})_ρ has finite orbit under Γ.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Theorem 1.4.2, p. 5; a special case of Theorem 7.2.1, p. 36
items.note: The version of the Putman–Wieland conjecture the paper actually proves for arbitrary H: it holds on the part of H₁(Σ_{g'}) spanned by irreducible representations of H of small dimension. It feeds the non-semisimple step of the main theorem through Lemma 8.6.1.

items.name: Canonical representations of free groups
items.statement: Let F_N be a free group on N generators with N = 2g or N = 2g + 1, and let ρ : F_N → GL_r(ℂ) be a representation whose conjugacy class has finite orbit under Out(F_N). If r < √(g+1), then ρ has finite image.
items.note: Deduced from Theorem 1.2.1 by choosing an isomorphism F_N ≅ π₁(Σ_{g,1}) for N even and F_N ≅ π₁(Σ_{g,2}) for N odd. Remark 1.6.3 makes it completely elementary through Nielsen's generators of Aut(F_N): if the N-tuples obtained from (A₁, …, A_N) by the cyclic permutation c, the transposition τ, the inversion ε : A₁ ↦ A₁⁻¹ and the Dehn twist d : (A₁, A₂, …) ↦ (A₁A₂, A₂, …) meet only finitely many conjugacy classes, then the A_i generate a finite subgroup of GL_r(ℂ). The same statement follows for characteristic quotients of free or surface groups (Remark 1.6.5).

items.name: Rank bound for sub-local systems of the first higher direct image of a unitary local system
items.statement: Let π : C → M be a smooth proper family of n-pointed curves of genus g with geometrically connected fibres such that the associated map M → M_{g,n} is dominant étale, and let π° : C° → M be the associated family of punctured curves. Let V be a unitary local system on C°. Then any nonzero sub-local system of R¹π°_*V has rank at least 2g − 2 rk V.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Theorem 1.7.1, p. 6; proved in §6.1, pp. 32–33
items.note: The main new technical input. In particular H⁰(M, R¹π°_*V) = 0 whenever g > rk V. It is proved by identifying the derivative of the period map of the variation of mixed Hodge structure on R¹π°_*V with a multiplication map of global sections (Theorem 5.1.6) and then applying the parabolic vector-bundle estimate of Proposition 5.2.3.

items.name: Family of n-pointed curves, versal family, punctured versal family
items.statement: Fix g, n ≥ 0 with n ≥ 1 if g = 1 and n ≥ 3 if g = 0, so that Σ_{g,n} is hyperbolic. For M a connected complex variety, a family of n-pointed curves of genus g over M is a smooth proper morphism π : C → M of relative dimension one with geometrically connected genus g fibres, equipped with n sections s₁, …, s_n : M → C with disjoint images. The family is versal if the induced map M → M_{g,n} is dominant and étale. With D := ⊔ᵢ im(sᵢ), C° := C \ D, j : C° ↪ C and π° := π ∘ j, the family π° : C° → M is the associated family of punctured curves, and a punctured versal family when π is versal. PMod_{g,n} = π₁(M_{g,n}) denotes the pure mapping class group, the index-n! subgroup of Mod_{g,n} fixing the punctures pointwise.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Notation 1.10.1 and Notation 1.10.3, pp. 10–11
items.note: The geometric setting of the whole paper: statements about MCG-finite representations of π₁(Σ_{g,n}) are converted into statements about local systems on the total space of a punctured versal family. Here M_{g,n} is the Deligne–Mumford moduli stack of n-pointed genus g smooth proper curves with geometrically connected fibres, and π₁ always means the topological fundamental group of the associated complex-analytic space or stack.

items.name: The adjoint local system and unitary representations
items.statement: For G an algebraic group with derived subgroup G^der and Lie algebra 𝔤^der, let Ad : G → GL(𝔤^der) be the conjugation action; for ρ : π₁(X, x) → G(ℂ) set ad(ρ) := Ad ∘ ρ. For ρ valued in GL_r(ℂ) or PGL_r(ℂ) this is the composite π₁(X, x) → GL(𝔭𝔤𝔩_r(ℂ)). If W is the local system attached to ρ, ad W is the local system attached to ad ρ. A representation π₁(X, x) → GL_r(ℂ) is unitary if its image has compact closure; equivalently, by averaging, if it preserves a positive-definite Hermitian form, i.e. is conjugate to a representation factoring through U(r). A complex local system is unitary if its monodromy representation is.
items.note: Both notions are used throughout: ad V is the local system whose first cohomology measures deformations, and unitarity is the property that non-abelian Hodge theory and the low-rank bound of [LL22, Theorem 1.2.12] deliver. Note that ad is taken with values in 𝔭𝔤𝔩_r, so that the determinant direction is discarded.

items.name: The Birman exact sequence and the fundamental group of the moduli stack of curves
items.statement: For m ∈ M_{g,n} a basepoint and m' ∈ M_{g,n+1} a lift of m there are isomorphisms π₁(M_{g,n}, m) ≅ PMod_{g,n} and π₁(M_{g,n+1}, m') ≅ PMod_{g,n+1} making the exact sequence of homotopy groups of the forgetful map M_{g,n+1} → M_{g,n}, namely 1 → π₁(Σ_{g,n}) → π₁(M_{g,n+1}, m') → π₁(M_{g,n}, m) → 1, agree with the Birman exact sequence 1 → π₁(Σ_{g,n}) → PMod_{g,n+1} → PMod_{g,n} → 1. The subgroup π₁(Σ_{g,n}) ⊂ PMod_{g,n+1} is the point-pushing subgroup.
items.note: The bridge between mapping class groups and geometry, used throughout. It follows from the contractibility of the universal cover of M_{g,n} (Teichmüller space) and the proper discontinuity of the PMod_{g,n}-action. A choice of homeomorphism between the reference surface and the Riemann surface at m is involved, and changing it conjugates the isomorphisms.

items.name: Closure properties of MCG-finite representations
items.statement: The direct sum and the tensor product of two MCG-finite representations of π₁(Σ_{g,n}) are MCG-finite, and any semisimple subquotient of an MCG-finite representation is MCG-finite.
items.note: The statement about semisimple subquotients is [LL19, Lemma 2.2.1]. It is what allows the induction on the socle filtration in §8.7: both the socle and the quotient by it are MCG-finite because the socle is a characteristic subrepresentation.

items.name: Restriction to the point-pushing subgroup is MCG-finite
items.statement: Let Γ ⊂ Mod_{g,n+1} be a finite-index subgroup containing the point-pushing subgroup π₁(Σ_{g,n}) ⊂ Mod_{g,n+1}, and let ρ : Γ → GL_r(ℂ) be a representation. Then ρ|_{π₁(Σ_{g,n})} is MCG-finite.
items.note: The proof is one line: for γ ∈ Γ, the representation ρ^γ(h) = ρ(γhγ⁻¹) equals ρ(γ)ρ(h)ρ(γ)⁻¹, so the image of Γ in PMod_{g,n} stabilises the conjugacy class of ρ. This is the source of the many known examples of MCG-finite representations — TQFT representations, Kodaira–Parshin representations — obtained by restricting representations of finite-index subgroups of the mapping class group.

items.name: Geometric counterpart: restriction to a fibre is MCG-finite
items.statement: Let π° : C° → M be a punctured versal family of n-pointed genus g curves, so that M → M_{g,n} is dominant and étale, let C° be a fibre of π°, and let ρ : π₁(C°) → GL_r(ℂ) be a representation of the fundamental group of the total space. Then ρ|_{π₁(C°)} is MCG-finite.
items.note: Proved in §2.1.6 from the exact sequence (2.1) and Lemma 2.1.4, by checking that the outer action of π₁(M) on π₁(C°) factors through the outer action of PMod_{g,n} coming from the Birman exact sequence. Closely related to [CH19, Theorem A1].

items.name: Dominant étale maps to the moduli stack have finite-index image on fundamental groups
items.statement: For M a scheme and any dominant étale map M → M_{g,n}, the image of π₁(M) → π₁(M_{g,n}) has finite index in π₁(M_{g,n}) ≅ PMod_{g,n}.
items.note: Reduced to a map of schemes by pulling back along a finite étale cover N → M_{g,n} that is a scheme, which exists by [PdJ95, Proposition 2.3.4], and then to [Deb01, Lemma 4.19]: pass to opens over which the map is finite flat and use that shrinking to opens preserves finiteness of the index.

items.name: Exactness of the homotopy sequence of a punctured versal family
items.statement: If C → M is a versal family of n-pointed curves of genus g with 3g − 3 + n ≥ 0 and C° is a fibre of π°, then the sequence 1 → π₁(C°) → π₁(C°) → π₁(M) → 1 is exact.
items.note: Only injectivity of π₁(C°) → π₁(C°) needs an argument; it holds in the universal case because the universal cover of M_{g,n} is contractible, and in general by pulling back along C° → C°_{g,n}.

items.name: The projective representation of a finite-index subgroup attached to an irreducible MCG-finite representation
items.statement: Let ρ be an irreducible MCG-finite representation of π₁(Σ_{g,n}, x), let Γ ⊂ PMod_{g,n} be the finite-index stabiliser of its conjugacy class and Γ̃ ⊂ PMod_{g,n+1} the preimage of Γ under the Birman surjection. Then there is a unique representation ρ̃ : Γ̃ → PGL_r(ℂ) whose restriction to the point-pushing subgroup π₁(Σ_{g,n}, x) ⊂ Γ̃ is the projectivisation of ρ. It is constructed by sending γ to the class of the matrix M_γ with M_γ ρ M_γ⁻¹ = γ(ρ), which is unique up to scalars by Schur's lemma.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Notation 2.2.1 and Lemma 2.2.2, pp. 14–15
items.note: This is the step that turns a representation of a surface group into a representation of a mapping class group, and is the reason cohomological rigidity on the total space of a family of curves can be used at all. A similar argument appears in the proof of [Sim92, Theorem 4].

items.name: Geometric form of the projective representation
items.statement: Let ρ : π₁(Σ_{g,n}, x) → GL_r(ℂ) be an irreducible MCG-finite representation. There exist a scheme M with a finite étale map M → M_{g,n}, with associated family of n-times punctured curves π° : C° → M, a point c ∈ C° with m = π°(c), and a representation ρ̃ : π₁(C°, c) → PGL_r(ℂ) such that, upon identifying π₁(Σ_{g,n}, x) ≅ π₁(C°_m, c), the projectivisation of ρ is ρ̃|_{π₁(C°_m,c)}.
items.note: The translation of Lemma 2.2.2 into the language of families, using Lemma 2.0.1. M is the finite étale cover of M_{g,n} attached to a finite-index subgroup of Γ, chosen to be a scheme rather than a Deligne–Mumford stack.

items.name: MCG-finite characters have finite image
items.statement: For g ≥ 1 and n ≥ 0, any MCG-finite representation ρ : π₁(Σ_{g,n}) → ℂ^× has finite image.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Proposition 2.3.1, pp. 15–16, quoting [BGMW17, Lemma 3.2]
items.note: The idea recalled in the paper: if a standard generator corresponding to a loop γ has infinite order under ρ, then acting on ρ by powers of the Dehn twist about γ gives infinitely many distinct representations. This is the rank-one case of the main theorem, and the input to the determinant statement of Lemma 2.3.2.

items.name: MCG-finite representations have finite determinant
items.statement: Let g ≥ 1 and let ρ : π₁(Σ_{g,n}) → GL_r(ℂ) be MCG-finite. Then det ρ has finite order. Moreover ρ factors through a subgroup G with SL_r(ℂ) ⊂ G ⊂ GL_r(ℂ) for which μ := G ∩ ker(GL_r(ℂ) → PGL_r(ℂ)) is finite.
items.note: Applies Proposition 2.3.1 to det ρ. The finiteness of μ is what makes the obstruction to lifting a PGL_r-representation to a GL_r-representation a class with coefficients in a finite abelian group, so that Lemma 2.3.3 can kill it.

items.name: Killing a finite abelian cohomology class by a dominant étale base change
items.statement: Let i > 0, let M be a complex variety, let μ be a finite abelian group and let σ ∈ H^i(π₁(M, m), μ). Then there is a dominant étale map M' → M with σ|_{M'} = 0 in H^i(π₁(M'), μ).
items.note: The technical device that allows the paper to replace M by a dominant étale cover whenever a finite lifting obstruction is in the way. It is used in Proposition 2.3.4 to lift ρ̃ from PGL_r to GL_r.

items.name: Lifting a projective representation on a family of curves to GL_r
items.statement: Let C → M be a versal family of n-pointed curves of genus g ≥ 1 with associated punctured family π° : C° → M, let c ∈ C°, m = π°(c), and suppose given ρ : π₁(C°_m, c) → GL_r(ℂ) and ρ̃ : π₁(C°, c) → PGL_r(ℂ) with ρ̃ restricting to the projectivisation of ρ, with ρ MCG-finite. Then there are a dominant étale map M' → M, the pulled-back punctured family C'°, and a representation ρ' : π₁(C'°, c') → GL_r(ℂ) lifting ρ̃ and restricting to ρ on the fibre through c'. Moreover im ρ' is contained in a subgroup G with SL_r(ℂ) ⊂ G ⊂ GL_r(ℂ) of finite index over SL_r(ℂ).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Proposition 2.3.4, pp. 16–18, diagrams (2.4) and (2.5)
items.note: Combines Lemma 2.3.2 with Lemma 2.3.3 applied to the finite abelian coefficient group μ. The conclusion about G is what gives ρ' finite determinant, needed for Mochizuki's Theorem 4.3.1 and for Lemma 2.4.1.

items.name: Every irreducible MCG-finite representation extends over a punctured versal family
items.statement: Let ρ : π₁(Σ_{g,n}) → GL_r(ℂ) be an irreducible MCG-finite representation with g ≥ 1. There exist a punctured versal family of curves C° → M and a representation ρ' of π₁(C°) whose determinant has finite order such that, for C° a fibre of π° and a suitable identification π₁(Σ_{g,n}) ≅ π₁(C°), one has ρ'|_{π₁(C°)} = ρ.
items.note: The partial converse to Proposition 2.1.3 and the form in which the geometric input is used in §8. Combined with Proposition 2.1.3 it reproves [CH19, Theorem A] for semisimple ρ when the flat bundle there is the Deligne canonical extension (Remark 2.3.6).

items.name: Unitarity and finiteness descend from an irreducible normal restriction
items.statement: Let H ⊴ G be a normal subgroup and ρ : G → GL_r(ℂ) a representation with det ρ of finite order such that ρ|_H is irreducible. If ρ|_H has finite image then ρ has finite image, and if ρ|_H is unitary then ρ is unitary.
items.note: The criterion that transfers fibral information to the total space of a family: applied with G = π₁(C°) and H = π₁(C°) it shows that a local system on C° whose fibral monodromy is unitary and irreducible is itself unitary, provided its determinant has finite order.

items.name: Structure of a family of local systems with unitary fibral restriction
items.statement: Let A be an Artin local ℂ-algebra with residue field ℂ, and let V be a local system of free A-modules on C° such that V|_{C°_m} is a constant deformation of a unitary local system, i.e. V|_{C°_m} ≅ V₀ ⊗_ℂ A for a unitary ℂ-local system V₀. Then there is a dominant étale map M' → M over which V|_{C'°} ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^s U_i ⊗ (π'°)^*W_i, with the W_i locally constant sheaves of free A-modules on M' and the U_i unitary local systems on C'°; for C'° a fibre, the U_i|_{C'°} are irreducible and pairwise non-isomorphic and W_i ≅ π'°_* Hom(U_i, V|_{C'°}).
items.note: Proved by applying Corollary 2.3.5 repeatedly to the irreducible summands of V₀ and checking that the natural evaluation map is an isomorphism fibrewise. This is the reduction that lets Theorem 6.2.1, which assumes unitarity only on fibres, be deduced from Theorem 1.7.1, which assumes it on the total space; it is also what splits f_*ℂ into isotypic pieces in the proof of Theorem 7.2.1.

items.name: Deformations with constant determinant are classified by the first cohomology of the adjoint
items.statement: Fix a group G and a representation ρ₀ : G → GL_r(ℂ). Let 0 → εA → A[ε]/ε² → A → 0 with A an Artin local ℂ-algebra, and let ρ_A : G → GL_r(A) be a deformation of ρ₀ over A with constant determinant. The set of equivalence classes of deformations of ρ_A to an A[ε]/ε²-representation with constant determinant is naturally in bijection with H¹(G, ad(ρ_A)), functorially in G.
items.note: The standard first-order deformation theory of a representation of an abstract group, stated with a fixed determinant so that the adjoint is taken in 𝔭𝔤𝔩_r rather than 𝔤𝔩_r. It is the reason all the vanishing theorems of §6 are stated for ad V.

items.name: Constancy of a first-order deformation on a normal subgroup
items.statement: Let 1 → N → G → Q → 1 be a short exact sequence of groups, let A be an Artin local ℂ-algebra and let ρ : G → GL_r(A) be a representation with H⁰(Q, H¹(N, ad(ρ)|_N)) = 0. If ρ_ε is any deformation of ρ to A[ε]/ε² with constant determinant, then ρ_ε|_N is equivalent to the constant deformation ρ ⊗_A A[ε]/ε²|_N.
items.note: The inductive step behind Proposition 3.2.1: the invariants H⁰(Q, H¹(N, ad)) are exactly the deformations of ρ|_N that are compatible with the G-action, and the vanishing hypothesis is supplied by Theorem 6.2.1.

items.name: A formal family with vanishing equivariant deformations is constant on the normal subgroup
items.statement: Let 1 → N → G → Q → 1 be a short exact sequence of groups and ρ₀ : G → GL_r(ℂ) a representation such that for all n and all deformations γ : G → GL_r(B_n) of ρ₀ with γ|_N constant one has H⁰(Q, H¹(N, ad(γ)|_N)) = 0. If ρ_∞ : G → GL_r(ℂ[[t]]) is any representation with ρ_∞ ≡ ρ₀ mod t and constant determinant, then ρ_∞|_N is conjugate to a constant representation: there exists M_∞ ∈ GL_r(ℂ[[t]]) with M_∞ ρ_∞|_N M_∞⁻¹ factoring through GL_r(ℂ).
items.note: The rigidity statement used in Lemma 8.5.1 to show that the non-abelian Hodge deformation of a low-rank MCG-finite local system does not move its restriction to a fibre. Here B_n runs over the Artin quotients ℂ[[t]]/t^n.

items.name: Polarizable complex variation of Hodge structure
items.statement: A complex PVHS on a smooth complex variety X is a complex local system with a decreasing filtration of the associated holomorphic bundle by holomorphic subbundles satisfying Griffiths transversality, together with a flat Hermitian pairing which polarizes the induced Hodge structure on each fibre; the paper refers to [LL22, §5] for the definitions and uses the associated bigrading on the flat bundle. A local system has a real structure if it is the complexification of a real orthogonal local system; V ⊕ V^∨ always has one.
items.note: The notion in which all the Hodge-theoretic input of the paper is phrased. Unitary local systems are exactly the complex PVHS with a one-step Hodge filtration, and the whole of §8 turns on the passage between the two.

items.name: Admissible graded-polarizable variation of mixed Hodge structure
items.statement: A variation of mixed Hodge structure on a smooth quasi-projective complex variety carries an increasing weight filtration by sub-local systems and a decreasing Hodge filtration by holomorphic subbundles satisfying Griffiths transversality, such that each graded piece of the weight filtration is a variation of pure Hodge structure; it is graded-polarizable if each graded piece is polarizable, and admissible if it has the relative monodromy filtration and the limiting behaviour required at the boundary of a compactification. The rational case is [PS08, Definitions 14.44, 14.45, 14.49]; the real case is [SZ85, Definition 3.4].
items.note: Admissibility is what makes the theorem of the fixed part (Theorem 4.2.1) available on a quasi-projective, non-proper base — which is essential here, since the base M is an open subvariety of the moduli of curves and the fibres are punctured.

items.name: Deligne canonical extension of a flat bundle with regular singularities
items.statement: For X a smooth variety with a normal crossings compactification X̄ with boundary D and (V ⊗ O_{X}, id ⊗ d) the flat bundle attached to a local system V on X, the Deligne canonical extension is the unique extension to a vector bundle with flat connection with logarithmic poles along D whose residues have eigenvalues with real parts in [0, 1). On a family of pointed curves it is denoted (ℰ, ∇) and is a vector bundle on C̄ with a flat connection with regular singularities along D.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Notation 5.1.1, pp. 27–28, following [Del70, Remarques 5.5(i)] and [LL22, Definition 4.1.2]
items.note: Every analytic statement in §§4–6 is made about the Deligne canonical extension: its restriction to a fibre carries the parabolic structure induced by the residues of ∇, which by Mehta–Seshadri is the parabolic bundle attached to the unitary local system on the fibre.

items.name: The variation of mixed Hodge structure on the first cohomology of a unitary local system
items.statement: Let V be a unitary local system on C° with real structure V_ℝ. Then R¹π°_*V_ℝ underlies an admissible graded-polarizable real variation of mixed Hodge structure with weights in [1, 2] and weight filtration W¹R¹π°_*V_ℝ := R¹π_*j_*V_ℝ ⊂ R¹π°_*V_ℝ =: W²R¹π°_*V_ℝ. Under the canonical identification R¹π°_*V ⊗ O_M ≅ R¹π_*(ℰ → ℰ ⊗ Ω¹_{C̄/M}(log D)) the Hodge filtration is the one induced by the filtration bête of the relative de Rham complex, that is F¹R¹π°_*V ⊗ O_M := im(π_*(ℰ ⊗ Ω¹_{C̄/M}(log D)) → R¹π°_*V ⊗ O_M).
items.note: Described by the authors as well known but hard to extract from the literature. Griffiths transversality is vacuous because the Hodge filtration has two steps; the pointwise statement is [Tim87, Theorem, p. 152] with the weight filtration from [Tim87, Lemma 6.2] and the Hodge filtration from the degeneration of the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence [Tim87, Theorem 7.1(a)]; graded-polarizability and admissibility come from Saito's theory of mixed Hodge modules [Sai90], [Sch19, Theorem 21.1], since Rj_*V_ℝ underlies an object of the derived category of real mixed Hodge modules.

items.name: The three-piece bigrading on the cohomology of a unitary local system
items.statement: For V a unitary local system on C° and H_V := R¹π°_*V ⊗ O_M with weight filtration W^•, Hodge filtration F^• and conjugate Hodge filtration F̄^• induced by H_V ≅ H_{V^∨}, set H_V^{1,0} := F¹ ∩ W¹, H_V^{0,1} := F̄¹ ∩ W¹ and H_V^{1,1} := F¹ ∩ F̄¹. Then H_V = H_V^{1,0} ⊕ H_V^{0,1} ⊕ H_V^{1,1}, and under the natural isomorphism H_V = H_V^∨ one has H_V^{i,j} = H_{V^∨}^{j,i}.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Lemma 4.1.2, p. 25 (equations (4.1) and (4.2), with Figure 3)
items.note: The bookkeeping that drives Lemma 6.1.1: an irreducible sub-local system L of R¹π°_*V either has its bigrading concentrated in degree (0,0), in which case the derivative of its period map vanishes, or supported on {(1,0),(0,1)}, in which case one of the two pieces has dimension at most rk L / 2.

items.name: Theorem of the fixed part for admissible graded-polarizable variations
items.statement: Let X be a smooth quasiprojective complex variety and W an admissible graded-polarizable real variation of mixed Hodge structure on X. Then there is a natural real Hodge structure on H⁰(X, W) such that the natural inclusion H⁰(X, W) ⊗ ℝ → W is a morphism of real variations of mixed Hodge structure.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Theorem 4.2.1, p. 26, quoting [SZ85, 4.19] and [PS08, 14.52]
items.note: The classical input from mixed Hodge theory. It is applied not to W itself but to the admissible variation L̃^∨ ⊗ W in the proof of Proposition 4.2.2.

items.name: The real form L̃ of a complex local system
items.statement: For L a complex local system on a variety, set L̃ := L if L admits a real structure and L̃ := L ⊕ L̄ otherwise. Then L̃ carries a natural real structure, and if L is irreducible and underlies a complex variation of Hodge structure and admits a real structure, then L underlies a real variation of Hodge structure.
items.note: A small but necessary device: the theorem of the fixed part is stated for real variations, while the local systems the paper produces are complex. The uniqueness of the complex variation carried by an irreducible local system, up to reindexing, forces the compatibility with complex conjugation.

items.name: A variant of the theorem of the fixed part for irreducible local systems
items.statement: Let X be a smooth quasiprojective complex variety, W an admissible graded-polarizable real variation of mixed Hodge structure on X, and L an irreducible complex local system on X with Hom(L, W_ℂ) ≠ 0. Then L̃ underlies a polarizable real variation of Hodge structure, and there exist a nonzero constant real mixed Hodge structure Q and a nonzero map of variations of mixed Hodge structure Q ⊗ L̃ → W.
items.note: Proved by decomposing gr^W_i W_ℂ = ⊕_j V_j ⊗ W_j with the V_j distinct irreducible local systems carrying polarizable complex variations [LL22, Proposition 4.1.4(2)], observing that L occurs among the V_j, and then taking Q := Hom(L̃, W) and applying Theorem 4.2.1. This is the form in which the fixed-part theorem enters Lemma 6.1.1.

items.name: Mochizuki's deformation of a representation to a complex variation of Hodge structure
items.statement: Let X̄ be a smooth projective variety, D ⊂ X̄ a strict normal crossings divisor and X = X̄ \ D. Any representation ρ : π₁(X) → GL_r(ℂ) with finite determinant admits a deformation with constant determinant to a representation underlying a complex PVHS.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Theorem 4.3.1, p. 27, quoting [Moc06, Theorem 10.5]
items.note: Non-abelian Hodge theory for quasi-projective varieties, generalising Simpson's projective case. The statement about determinants is not in [Moc06] verbatim and is obtained by examining the proof. This is the main external input to the semisimple case, Theorem 8.5.3: even when n = 0 and π° is proper, the total space C° is not, so the quasi-projective theory is needed.

items.name: Cohomologically rigid semisimple representations underlie complex variations of Hodge structure
items.statement: With X̄, D, X as above, let ρ : π₁(X) → GL_r(ℂ) be semisimple with finite determinant and H¹(X, ad ρ) = 0. Then ρ underlies a complex PVHS.
items.note: Proved by taking G the Zariski closure of im ρ, which is reductive, noting that its Lie algebra is a summand of ad ρ so that ρ is cohomologically rigid as a G-representation, and then applying [Moc06, Lemma 10.13] together with rigidity to see that the deformation is trivial. This is the step in Proposition 8.4.1 that makes every Galois conjugate of an integral MCG-finite representation unitary.

items.name: The analytic setting for the period map, and Hodge–de Rham degeneration for unitary coefficients
items.statement: Let π : C̄ → B be a relative smooth proper curve over a smooth contractible complex-analytic base B with disjoint sections s₁, …, s_n with images D, C° = C̄ \ D, π° : C° → B, V a unitary ℂ-local system on C°, W := R¹π°_*V, and (ℰ, ∇) the Deligne canonical extension. Set H := W ⊗_ℂ O_B ≅ R¹π_*(ℰ → ℰ ⊗ Ω¹_{C̄/B}(log D)), carrying the Gauss–Manin connection. Because V is unitary the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence degenerates, giving the two-step filtration F¹H := π_*(ℰ ⊗ Ω¹_{C̄/B}(log D)) and H/F¹H ≅ R¹π_*ℰ.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Notation 5.1.1 and §5.1.2, pp. 27–28, equation (5.1)
items.note: Degeneration is [Tim87, Theorem 7.1(a)], with [Sai88, Théorème 5.3.1] as a far more general reference. The paper writes Ω¹_{C̄/B}(D) for the isomorphic Ω¹_{C̄/B}(log D) and identifies Ω¹_{C̄/B} with the relative dualizing sheaf ω_{C̄/B} without comment (Remark 5.1.3).

items.name: The period map of the first cohomology of a unitary local system
items.statement: Since B is contractible the local system W can be globally trivialized, giving a flat trivialization of H and hence a period map P : B → Gr(rk F¹H, rk H) to the Grassmannian of subspaces, sending b to F¹H_b ⊂ H_b.
items.note: The object whose derivative is computed in Theorem 5.1.6. Contractibility of B is why the paper works analytically-locally on the base and only afterwards globalises through the theorem of the fixed part.

items.name: The derivative of the period map and the classifying map of the family
items.statement: The derivative of P is the O_B-linear map dP : T_B → P^*T_{Gr} ≅ (F¹H)^∨ ⊗ (H/F¹H), dual to dP^∨ : F¹H ⊗ (H/F¹H)^∨ → Ω¹_B. Since C̄, s₁, …, s_n is a family of n-pointed curves over B there is also a classifying map c : B → M_{g,n} with pullback c^* : c^*Ω¹_{M_{g,n}} → Ω¹_B. At a point b, writing C = C̄_b, D = D_b, E = ℰ|_C, Serre duality identifies dP^∨_b with a map H⁰(C, E ⊗ Ω¹_C(log D)) ⊗ H⁰(C, E^∨ ⊗ ω_C) → Ω¹_{B,b} and c^*_b with a map H⁰(C, ω_C^{⊗2}(D)) → Ω¹_{B,b}.
items.note: The identification of the tangent space of the Grassmannian is [EH16, Theorem 3.5] together with the fact that the universal sub- and quotient bundles pull back to F¹H and H/F¹H. Serre duality on the fibre is what converts the abstract derivative into a multiplication of global sections.

items.name: The Gauss–Manin composite ∇ : F¹H → H/F¹H ⊗ Ω¹_B
items.statement: Let ∇ be the O_B-linear map obtained as the composition F¹H ↪ H →^{∇_GM} H ⊗ Ω¹_B → H/F¹H ⊗ Ω¹_B. Its fibre at m ∈ M is written ∇_m, and for v ∈ F¹H_m the induced linear map ∇_m(v) : H⁰(C, E^∨ ⊗ ω_C) → H⁰(C, ω_C^{⊗2}(D)) is u ↦ B_E(v, u).
items.note: This O_B-linear shadow of the Gauss–Manin connection is the concrete object the whole argument manipulates: a low-rank sub-local system of R¹π°_*V produces a vector v with ∇_m(v) of small rank, and Proposition 5.2.3 forbids that unless rk V is large.

items.name: The derivative of the period map is multiplication of global sections followed by the trace
items.statement: Under the identifications above, dP^∨_b factors as the tensor product of global sections H⁰(C, E ⊗ Ω¹_C(log D)) ⊗ H⁰(C, E^∨ ⊗ ω_C) → H⁰(C, E ⊗ E^∨ ⊗ ω_C^{⊗2}(D)) followed by the map tr induced by the trace pairing E ⊗ E^∨ → O_C into H⁰(C, ω_C^{⊗2}(D)) and then by c^*_b. Moreover dP^∨_b is adjoint to ∇_b.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Theorem 5.1.6, p. 29, diagram (5.4); proved in Appendix A
items.note: The generalisation, to a unitary local system on a punctured curve, of the classical identification of the derivative of the period map of H¹(C, ℂ) with the multiplication map H⁰(C, ω) ⊗ H⁰(C, ω) → H⁰(C, ω^{⊗2}) [Voi07, Lemma 10.22]. The proof in Appendix A follows [Voi07, §§9–10].

items.name: The bilinear pairing B_E on a vector bundle over a pointed curve
items.statement: Let C be a smooth proper connected curve of genus g, D ⊂ C a reduced divisor and E a vector bundle on C. Then B_E : (E ⊗ ω_C(D)) × (E^∨ ⊗ ω_C) → ω_C^{⊗2}(D) is the perfect pairing given by the tensor product followed by the trace pairing E ⊗ E^∨ → O_C.
items.note: The pairing whose induced map on global sections computes the derivative of the period map by Theorem 5.1.6. Proposition 5.2.3 is a lower bound for rk E in terms of the rank of B_E(v, −) on global sections, and is the source of the √(g+1) in the main theorem.

items.name: Parabolic bundles, parabolic degree, slope and semistability
items.statement: A parabolic bundle on (C, D) with D = x₁ + ⋯ + x_n is a vector bundle E on C together with, for each j, a decreasing filtration E_{x_j} = E¹_j ⊋ ⋯ ⊋ E^{n_j+1}_j = 0 and an increasing sequence of weights 0 ≤ α¹_j < ⋯ < α^{n_j}_j < 1. With J the set of j for which α¹_j = 0, put Ê₀ := ker(E → ⊕_{j∈J} E_{x_j}/E²_j), a subbundle of E. The parabolic degree is par-deg(E_⋆) := deg(E) + Σ_j Σ_i α^i_j dim(E^i_j/E^{i+1}_j) and the parabolic slope is μ_⋆(E_⋆) := par-deg(E_⋆)/rk(E). A subbundle F ⊂ E inherits a parabolic structure by intersecting the filtrations and taking maximal weights, and E_⋆ is parabolically semistable if μ_⋆(F_⋆) ≤ μ_⋆(E_⋆) for every nonzero subbundle F.
items.note: The paper gives a lightning review and refers to [LL22, §2] and [BY96, Definition 2.3] for the coparabolic generality. The construction Ê₀, taking the kernel of the evaluation at the points with weight zero, is the only piece of that generality needed here.

items.name: The Mehta–Seshadri correspondence
items.statement: Mehta and Seshadri give a correspondence between parabolically stable parabolic bundles of parabolic degree zero on (C, D) and irreducible unitary local systems on C \ D. The bijection sends a local system V to the Deligne canonical extension of (V ⊗ O, id ⊗ d) with the parabolic structure induced by the connection.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), §5.2.1, p. 30, quoting [MS80, Theorem 4.1, Remark 4.3]
items.note: Remark 5.2.2 notes that it is not entirely trivial to extract from [MS80] that the parabolic bundle constructed there is the one attached to the Deligne canonical extension; what the paper actually uses is that the parabolic bundle of the canonical extension is parabolically semistable, which follows from [Sim90, Theorem 5], with the generalisation to complex PVHS explained in [AHL19, §5].

items.name: Low rank of the pairing forces high rank of the bundle
items.statement: Let E_⋆ be a semistable parabolic bundle on (C, D) of parabolic degree zero with underlying bundle E, and let v ∈ H⁰(C, E ⊗ ω_C(D)) be a nonzero global section such that the map H⁰(C, E^∨ ⊗ ω_C) → H⁰(C, ω_C^{⊗2}(D)), u ↦ B_E(v, u), has rank r. Then rk(E) ≥ g − r.
items.note: Proved by applying Proposition 5.2.4(II) to the parabolic bundle (E_⋆)^∨ ⊗ ω_C(D), which has parabolic slope 2g − 2 + n, with U the kernel of the map of bundles induced by B_E(v, −), so that c = 1 and δ = r. This is the geometric heart of the rank bound.

items.name: The parabolic Clifford-type estimate
items.statement: Let C be a smooth proper connected genus g curve and E_⋆ = (E, {E^i_j}, {α^i_j}) a nonzero parabolically semistable parabolic bundle with respect to D = x₁ + ⋯ + x_n. Let U ⊂ Ê₀ be a subbundle, c := rk E − rk U and δ := h⁰(C, Ê₀) − h⁰(C, U). If μ_⋆(E_⋆) > 2g − 2 + n then rk E > gc − δ, and if μ_⋆(E_⋆) = 2g − 2 + n then rk E ≥ gc − δ.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Proposition 5.2.4, p. 31, quoting [LL22, Proposition 6.3.6]
items.note: Taken as a black box, with [LL22, Proposition 6.3.1] as a less technical variant. Remark 5.2.5 records the translation between the stated form and the coparabolic form in [LL22], using that E_⋆ is parabolically stable if and only if Ê_⋆ is coparabolically stable, with equal slopes. Ultimately it rests on Clifford's theorem for vector bundles on curves.

items.name: A low-rank sub-local system produces a vector with degenerate Gauss–Manin derivative
items.statement: Let π° : C° → M be a punctured versal family of genus g curves and V a unitary local system on C°, and let ∇_m be the fibre at m of ∇ : F¹H → H/F¹H ⊗ Ω_M. If L ⊂ R¹π°_*V is a nonzero irreducible sub-local system, then after possibly replacing V and L by their complex conjugates there is a nonzero v ∈ L_m ∩ F¹H_m such that ∇_m(v) has rank at most (rk L)/2.
items.note: Essentially an application of the theorem of the fixed part in the form of Proposition 4.2.2: one gets a nonzero map of variations Q ⊗ L̃ → R¹π°_*V, and since the bigrading of R¹π°_*V is supported in degrees (1,0), (0,1), (1,1) either the bigrading of L is concentrated in degree (0,0), whence ∇(v) = 0, or it is supported on {(1,0),(0,1)}, whence dim L_m/F¹L_m ≤ (rk L)/2.

items.name: Vanishing of global sections of the first higher direct image with Artinian coefficients
items.statement: Let π° : C° → M be a punctured versal family of genus g curves, m ∈ M, C° = C°_m, A a local Artin ℂ-algebra with residue field ℂ, and V a locally constant sheaf of free A-modules on C° such that V|_{C°} is a constant deformation of a unitary local system, i.e. V|_{C°} ≅ V₀ ⊗ A for a unitary complex local system V₀, and rk_A V < g. Then H⁰(M, R¹π°_*V) = 0.
items.note: The workhorse of §8: unitarity is only assumed on fibres, at the cost of ruling out trivial sub-local systems rather than arbitrary low-rank ones. It is deduced from Theorem 1.7.1 by passing to a dominant étale cover and writing V as ⊕ U_i ⊗ (π°)^*W_i with the U_i unitary (Lemma 2.4.2): a nonzero global section of R¹π°_*(U ⊗ (π°)^*W) = (R¹π°_*U) ⊗ W gives a nonzero map W^∨ → R¹π°_*U and hence a sub-local system of rank less than 2g − 2 rk U, contradicting Theorem 1.7.1.

items.name: Higher Prym representations and isotypic components
items.statement: Let Σ_g be an oriented genus g surface and Σ_{g,b,p} the complement of b disjoint open discs and p disjoint points, and let PMod_{g,b,p} be the subgroup of its mapping class group fixing the punctures and boundary components pointwise. Fix a basepoint v₀, counted as an extra puncture, so that PMod_{g,b,p+1} acts on π₁(Σ_{g,b,p}, v₀). Let K ⊴ π₁(Σ_{g,b,p}, v₀) be a finite-index normal subgroup with quotient a finite group H, corresponding to a Galois cover Σ_{g',b',p'} → Σ_{g,b,p} and a surjection ϕ, and let Γ ⊂ PMod_{g,b,p+1} be the finite-index subgroup preserving ϕ up to conjugacy. For ρ an irreducible H-representation, H₁(Σ_{g',b',p'}, ℂ)_ρ := ρ ⊗ Hom_H(ρ, H₁(Σ_{g',b',p'}, ℂ)) is the ρ-isotypic component. Filling in the punctures and discs gives the action of Γ on V_K := H₁(Σ_{g'}, ℂ), the higher Prym representation.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Notation 7.1.1, p. 35, following [PW13, pp. 80–81]
items.note: The representations the Putman–Wieland conjecture is about. The isotypic decomposition is H-equivariant and Γ-stable, and the paper's theorem is proved one isotypic component at a time, which is why the bound depends on dim ρ rather than on #H.

items.name: The Putman–Wieland property and the Putman–Wieland conjecture
items.statement: Fix a finite group H and g, b, p ≥ 0. PW^H_{g,b,p} is the statement that for every surjection ϕ : π₁(Σ_{g,b,p}, v₀) ↠ H with K := ker ϕ, every nonzero vector v ∈ V_K has infinite orbit under Γ. The Putman–Wieland conjecture asserts that PW^H_{g,b,p} holds for every finite group H whenever g ≥ 2, b ≥ 0, p ≥ 0.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Definition 7.1.2 and Conjecture 7.1.3, p. 35, restating [PW13, Conjecture 1.2]
items.note: Remark 7.1.4 notes that [PW13] states the conjecture without a group H and with ℚ coefficients; the version here is equivalent and more convenient. Remark 7.1.5 records that there is a counterexample when g = 2 [Mar, Theorem 1.3], so the hypothesis g ≥ 2 is not enough and an asymptotic statement in g is the right target.

items.name: No small invariant subrepresentations in an isotypic component
items.statement: With the notation above, let ρ be an irreducible complex H-representation and Γ' ⊂ Γ a finite-index subgroup. Then H¹(Σ_{g',b',p'}, ℂ)_ρ has no nonzero Γ'-invariant subrepresentation of dimension strictly less than 2g − 2 dim ρ, and the same holds for H₁(Σ_{g'}, ℂ)_ρ.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Theorem 7.2.1, p. 36; proved in §7.3, pp. 37–38
items.note: The paper's main contribution to the Putman–Wieland conjecture. Remark 7.2.2 stresses that subrepresentations, not arbitrary subquotients, are meant: for b' + p' > 0 the Γ-representation H¹(Σ_{g',b',p'}, ℂ) need not be semisimple. The proof applies Theorem 1.7.1 to the local systems U_ρ appearing in the decomposition of f_*ℂ for a versal family of ϕ-covers, and then descends from H¹(Σ_{g',n'}) to H₁(Σ_{g'}) using Poincaré duality and the intersection pairing.

items.name: Putman–Wieland for groups all of whose irreducible representations are small
items.statement: PW^H_{g,b,p} holds for every finite group H such that every irreducible representation ρ of H has dim ρ < g.
items.note: If dim ρ < g then 2g − 2 dim ρ > 1, so by Theorem 7.2.1 no isotypic component has a nonzero Γ'-invariant line; a vector with finite orbit would give a finite-index subgroup with a fixed vector.

items.name: Putman–Wieland for groups of order less than g²
items.statement: For fixed g, b, p ≥ 0, PW^H_{g,b,p} holds for every finite group H with #H < g².
items.note: Because #H is the sum of the squares of the degrees of the irreducible characters [FH91, (2.19)], the hypothesis #H < g² forces every irreducible representation of H to have dimension less than g, and Corollary 7.2.3 applies.

items.name: Reduction of the Putman–Wieland statement to surfaces without boundary
items.statement: With the notation of Notation 7.1.1, for any g ≥ 0, b, p ≥ 0, ρ an irreducible H-representation and Γ' ⊂ Γ of finite index, there are a finite-index subgroup Γ'' ⊂ PMod_{g,0,b+p+1} and an isomorphism H₁(Σ_{g',b',p'}, ℂ)_ρ → H₁(Σ_{g,0,b'+p'}, ℂ)_ρ carrying Γ'-invariant subspaces bijectively to Γ''-invariant subspaces.
items.note: Shrinking boundary components to punctures is a deformation retraction, and the kernel of PMod_{g,b,p} → PMod_{g,0,b+p} is generated by the ℤ^b of boundary rotations [FM12, Theorem 3.18], which acts trivially on homology.

items.name: Versal family of ϕ-covers
items.statement: Given a surjection ϕ : π₁(Σ_{g,0,n}, v₀) ↠ H, a versal family of ϕ-covers is the data of a dominant étale morphism M → M_{g,n} with associated punctured family π° : C° → M, a point c ∈ C° with m = π°(c), C° = C°_m and an identification i : π₁(Σ_{g,0,n}, v₀) ≅ π₁(C°, c), and a finite étale Galois H-cover f : X° → C° inducing π₁(C°, c) → π₁(C°, c)/π₁(X°, x) ≅ H agreeing with ϕ under i.
items.note: Existence is [Wew98, Theorem 4], which produces M as a Deligne–Mumford stack whose points have isotropy the centre of H; the paper replaces it by a scheme with a dominant étale map to it, and passes to a further cover so that π° admits a section and M → M_{g,n} lifts to M → M_{g,n+1}.

items.name: Cohomological rigidity and strong cohomological rigidity
items.statement: Let X̄ be a smooth projective variety, Z ⊂ X̄ a strict normal crossings divisor and X = X̄ \ Z, let G be a reductive group over ℂ and ρ : π₁(X) → G(ℂ) a homomorphism with quasi-unipotent monodromy at infinity. Then ρ is cohomologically rigid if H¹(X̄, j_{!*} ad ρ) = 0, where j : X ↪ X̄ and j_{!*} is the intermediate extension. If H¹(X, ad ρ) = 0 then ρ is strongly cohomologically rigid. A local system is (strongly) cohomologically rigid if its monodromy representation is.
items.note: For irreducible ρ, cohomological rigidity says that ρ is a smooth isolated point of the character variety parametrising representations with fixed local monodromy at infinity [KP20b, Proposition 4.7, Remark 4.8]. When X̄ is a curve j_{!*} = j_*.

items.name: Strong cohomological rigidity implies cohomological rigidity
items.statement: In the setting of Definition 8.1.1, if H¹(X, ad ρ) = 0 then ρ is cohomologically rigid.
items.note: Uses the identification H¹(X̄, j_{!*} ad ρ) ≅ H¹(U, a_* ad ρ) for a suitable dense open U ⊂ X̄ containing X [EG18, Remark 2.4], [KP20b, Remark 4.8], and the injection H¹(U, a_* ad ρ) ↪ H¹(X, ad ρ) from the Leray spectral sequence. It is how the paper always verifies rigidity in practice.

items.name: Low-rank local systems with irreducible unitary fibres are strongly cohomologically rigid
items.statement: Let V be a GL_r- (respectively PGL_r-) local system on C° with r < √(g+1) such that for m ∈ M the restriction V|_{C°} is (respectively is the projectivisation of) an irreducible unitary local system. Then V is strongly cohomologically rigid, hence cohomologically rigid.
items.note: Proved by the Leray spectral sequence of π°: it suffices that H⁰(M, R¹π°_* ad V) = H¹(M, π°_* ad V) = 0. The first vanishes by Theorem 6.2.1 with A = ℂ, since rk ad V = r² − 1 < g; the second because ad V has no invariants on the fibre, by irreducibility, so π°_* ad V = 0. This is the exact place where the bound r < √(g+1) is used.

items.name: Integral representations and local systems
items.statement: Let G be a group scheme over ℤ. A representation π₁(X, x) → G(ℂ) is integral if it is conjugate to a representation factoring through G(O_K) for some number field K; a local system on a connected space is integral if its monodromy representation is.
items.note: Used for G = GL_r and G = PGL_r. Integrality is the hinge of the argument: once the representation is defined over O_K, compactness of the unitary group and discreteness of O_K reduce finiteness of the image to unitarity of every Galois conjugate.

items.name: Dehn twists act quasi-unipotently in linear representations of finite-index subgroups
items.statement: Suppose g ≥ 3, γ ⊂ Σ_{g,n} is a simple closed curve and Γ ⊂ Mod_{g,n} is a finite-index subgroup with Dehn twist δ_γ. Then for m with δ_γ^m ∈ Γ and any representation ρ : Γ → GL_r(ℂ), the matrix ρ(δ_γ^m) is quasi-unipotent.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Proposition 8.3.2, p. 40, quoting [AS16, Proposition 2.4]
items.note: The input needed to check the quasi-unipotent local monodromy hypothesis of the Klevdal–Patrikis integrality theorem: boundary monodromy of a strict normal crossings compactification of C° corresponds to products of commuting Dehn twists, and products of commuting quasi-unipotent matrices are quasi-unipotent.

items.name: Integrality of cohomologically rigid local systems
items.statement: A cohomologically rigid local system with quasi-unipotent local monodromy at the boundary of a strict normal crossings compactification of a smooth quasi-projective complex variety, with values in a group with trivial abelianisation, is integral.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Used at p. 40 in the proof of Lemma 8.3.3, quoting [KP20b, Theorem 1.2], which builds on [EG18]
items.note: The arithmetic input to the whole paper. It rests on Lafforgue's work on the Langlands correspondence for function fields and on the resulting cases of Deligne's companion conjectures. The paper applies it to the PGL_r-local system attached to ρ̃, where the abelianisation of PGL_r(ℂ) is trivial.

items.name: The projectivisation of a low-rank unitary MCG-finite representation is integral
items.statement: Let g ≥ 3 and let ρ : π₁(Σ_{g,n}) → GL_r(ℂ) be an irreducible, unitary, MCG-finite representation with r < √(g+1). Then the composite Pρ : π₁(Σ_{g,n}) → GL_r(ℂ) → PGL_r(ℂ) is integral.
items.note: Applies Proposition 8.2.1 to the PGL_r-local system attached to ρ̃ from Lemma 2.2.3, then the Klevdal–Patrikis theorem. The quasi-unipotence hypothesis is checked by building a strict normal crossings compactification of C°: C° is a finite étale cover of M_{g,n+1}, one blows up boundary strata of the Deligne–Mumford compactification M̄_{g,n+1} to get a strict normal crossings compactification, takes the normalisation of C° in it, and uses [LLSS20, Lemma 2.1.1] together with Proposition 8.3.2.

items.name: A low-rank unitary MCG-finite representation is integral
items.statement: Let g ≥ 3 and let ρ : π₁(Σ_{g,n}) → GL_r(ℂ) be an irreducible, unitary, MCG-finite representation with r < √(g+1). Then ρ is integral.
items.note: Lifts the integrality of Lemma 8.3.3 from PGL_r to GL_r, using that det ρ has finite order (Lemma 2.3.2) and that the kernel μ of GL_r → PGL_r meets the image in a finite group.

items.name: Low-rank unitary MCG-finite representations have finite image
items.statement: Let ρ : π₁(Σ_{g,n}) → GL_r(ℂ) be a unitary MCG-finite representation with r < √(g+1). Then ρ has finite image.
items.note: Step 1 of the proof of the main theorem. After Lemma 8.3.4 one has ρ valued in GL_r(O_K); for each embedding τ : O_K ↪ ℂ, the extension ρ'_τ over a punctured versal family is irreducible with finite determinant and strongly cohomologically rigid, since strong cohomological rigidity is preserved by automorphisms of ℂ, so ρ'_τ underlies a complex PVHS by Lemma 4.3.2 and ρ_τ is unitary by [LL22, Theorem 1.2.12]. A representation into GL_r(O_K) that is unitary at every embedding has finite image by [LL22, Lemma 7.2.1].

items.name: A formal deformation with unitary special fibre is fibrewise constant
items.statement: Let π° : C° → M be a punctured versal family of genus g curves, c ∈ C°, m = π°(c), C° = C°_m, and let ρ_∞ : π₁(C°, c) → GL_r(ℂ[[t]]) be a representation with r < √(g+1) and constant determinant such that ρ₀ := ρ_∞ ⊗ ℂ restricted to π₁(C°, c) is unitary. Then ρ_∞|_{π₁(C°,c)} is conjugate to a constant representation.
items.note: Proposition 3.2.1 applied to the exact sequence 1 → π₁(C°) → π₁(C°) → π₁(M) → 1 of Lemma 2.1.5, with the hypothesis H⁰(π₁(M), H¹(π₁(C°), ad γ)) = 0 supplied by Theorem 6.2.1 over the Artin quotients ℂ[[t]]/t^n.

items.name: Constancy of the fibral restriction over a finite-type base
items.statement: Let π° : C° → M be a punctured versal family of genus g curves, c ∈ C°, m = π°(c), C° = C°_m, X a finite-type connected ℂ-scheme and ρ : π₁(C°, c) → GL_r(O_X(X)) a representation with r < √(g+1) and constant determinant. If there is a closed point y ∈ X with residue field ℂ such that ρ_y|_{π₁(C°,c)} is unitary, then for every closed point x ∈ X the representation ρ_x|_{π₁(C°,c)} is conjugate to ρ_y|_{π₁(C°,c)}.
items.note: Reduces to a curve X, applies Lemma 8.5.1 at y to see that the image of a dense open lies in the GL_r(ℂ)-orbit of ρ_y|_{π₁(C°)}, and closes up using that the orbit of a semisimple, hence of a unitary, representation is closed in the representation variety [Sik12, Theorem 30]. This is what shows that the non-abelian Hodge deformation of §8.5 did not move the restriction to a fibre.

items.name: The semisimple case of the main theorem
items.statement: Let ρ : π₁(Σ_{g,n}) → GL_r(ℂ) be a semisimple MCG-finite representation with r < √(g+1). Then ρ has finite image.
items.note: Step 2. One may assume ρ irreducible. Corollary 2.3.5 gives a local system V with finite determinant on the total space of a punctured versal family restricting to ρ on a fibre; Theorem 4.3.1 deforms V with constant determinant to a local system V₀ underlying a complex PVHS; since r < 2√(g+1), [LL22, Theorem 1.2.12] makes V₀|_{C°} unitary, and it is MCG-finite by Proposition 2.1.3, so it has finite monodromy by Proposition 8.4.1; finally V|_{C°} = V₀|_{C°} by Lemma 8.5.2. The acknowledgements record that Hélène Esnault found and helped correct a substantial gap in the original proof of this theorem.

items.name: Splitting of low-rank extensions of MCG-finite representations
items.statement: Let ρ be an MCG-finite representation of π₁(Σ_{g,n}) and ρ₁ ⊂ ρ a semisimple characteristic subrepresentation with ρ₂ = ρ/ρ₁ also semisimple. If ρ₁ and ρ₂ have finite image and rk ρ < √(g+1), then ρ has finite image, i.e. the extension of ρ₂ by ρ₁ splits.
items.note: Step 3, the only place where the Putman–Wieland results are used. Decomposing ρ₂^∨ ⊗ ρ₁ ≅ ⊕ σ_i^{⊕n_i} and using the AM–GM inequality gives n_i · dim σ_i < (g + 1)/4. Passing to a finite Galois cover Σ_{g',n'} on which ρ₁ and ρ₂ trivialise, the extension class becomes an H-equivariant map H₁(Σ_{g',n'}) → ρ₂^∨ ⊗ ρ₁, hence a Γ-stable subspace Q_i ⊂ H¹(Σ_{g',n'})_{σ_i} of rank at most (g+1)/4; but Theorem 7.2.1 forces any nonzero such subspace to have rank at least 2g − 2 dim σ_i > 3g/2 − 1/2 > (g+1)/4, so Q_i = 0.

items.name: Closed orbits of semisimple representations in the representation variety
items.statement: In the representation variety Hom(π₁(X), GL_r(ℂ)) with its conjugation action, the GL_r(ℂ)-orbit of a semisimple representation is closed.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Used at p. 43 in the proof of Lemma 8.5.2, quoting [Sik12, Theorem 30]
items.note: A standard fact of geometric invariant theory for character varieties. It is what lets a statement proved on a dense open subset of the base be propagated to the whole base.

items.name: Low-rank complex variations of Hodge structure on a very general curve are unitary
items.statement: A complex PVHS of rank less than 2√(g+1) on a punctured versal family of genus g curves restricts to a unitary local system on a fibre, and a local system on an analytically very general curve underlying an integral PVHS has finite monodromy whenever its rank is less than 2√(g+1).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Used at pp. 41–43 and p. 46, quoting [LL22, Theorem 1.2.12] and [LL22, Corollary 1.2.7]
items.note: The authors' earlier semistability results for isomonodromic deformations, taken here as external input. They are the reason the paper's bounds are of the shape √(g+1), and the reason the conjectural improvement to 2√(g+1) in Remark 9.1.5 is plausible for semisimple representations.

items.name: Representations into GL_r of a ring of integers that are unitary at every place have finite image
items.statement: Let ρ : π₁(Σ_{g,n}) → GL_r(O_K) be a representation such that ρ ⊗_{O_K, τ} ℂ is unitary for every embedding τ : O_K ↪ ℂ. Then ρ has finite image.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Used at p. 41 in the proof of Proposition 8.4.1, quoting [LL22, Lemma 7.2.1]
items.note: A Burnside-style argument: the image lies in a discrete subgroup of a product of compact unitary groups, hence is finite. It is the final step that converts integrality plus unitarity at all embeddings into finiteness.

items.name: Arithmetic representations of the geometric étale fundamental group
items.statement: Let X be a variety over a finitely generated field K with algebraic closure K̄, and let ρ : π₁^ét(X_{K̄}) → GL_r(ℚ̄_ℓ) be a continuous representation. Then ρ is arithmetic if its conjugacy class has finite orbit under the action of Gal(K̄/K) on isomorphism classes of π₁^ét(X_{K̄})-representations, induced by the natural outer action of Gal(K̄/K) on π₁^ét(X_{K̄}).
items.note: The arithmetic analogue of MCG-finiteness, and the hypothesis in the relative Fontaine–Mazur conjecture: the relative form of that conjecture predicts that all semisimple arithmetic representations are of geometric origin [Pet20, Conjecture 1 bis].

items.name: The arithmetic homotopy exact sequence and the outer Galois action
items.statement: For C° a smooth n-punctured geometrically connected curve over a finitely generated field K of characteristic zero, the sequences 1 → π₁^ét(C°_{K̄}) → π₁^ét(C°) → Gal(K̄/K) → 1 and its analogue over the moduli stack are exact, because the étale fundamental group is the profinite completion of the topological fundamental group and profinite completion preserves exactness of a short exact sequence whose left term has trivial centre.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), §9.1, pp. 46–47, quoting [GR71, Exposé XII, Corollaire 5.2] and [And74, Proposition 3]
items.note: The formal input to the proof of Theorem 9.1.2. The two exact sequences, for Spec K and for M_{g,n,ℚ̄}, induce compatible outer actions on π₁^ét(C°_{K̄}), and since Spec K → M_{g,n,ℚ̄} is dominant, the outer action of π₁(Spec K) factors through that of π₁(M_{g,n,ℚ̄}) with image of finite index.

items.name: Density of the topological fundamental group in the étale fundamental group of a curve
items.statement: For a smooth punctured curve over ℂ, the topological fundamental group of the associated Riemann surface injects into and is dense in the étale fundamental group, by residual finiteness of surface groups and the comparison of étale and topological fundamental groups; consequently a continuous representation of the étale fundamental group has finite image as soon as its restriction to the topological fundamental group does.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), §9.1, p. 47, quoting [GR71, Exposé XII, Corollaire 5.2]
items.note: The bridge that lets the topological Theorem 1.2.1 be applied to an ℓ-adic representation after choosing an embedding K ↪ ℂ and an isomorphism ℚ̄_ℓ ≅ ℂ.

items.name: Arithmetic representations of low rank on a generic curve have finite image
items.statement: Let K be a finitely generated field of characteristic zero and (C, x₁, …, x_n) a smooth n-pointed geometrically connected curve of genus g over K such that Spec(K) → M_{g,n,ℚ̄} factors through the generic point. If r < √(g+1), then any continuous arithmetic representation ρ : π₁^ét(C_{K̄} \ {x₁, …, x_n}) → GL_r(ℚ̄_ℓ) has finite image.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Theorem 9.1.2, p. 45; proved at the end of §9.1, pp. 46–47
items.note: A prediction of the relative Fontaine–Mazur conjecture, verified in this range: not only are such representations of geometric origin, they have finite image. Remark 9.1.3 draws the consequence that arithmetic representations are not Zariski-dense in the ℚ̄_ℓ-points of the character variety of semisimple rank-r representations for 1 < r < √(g+1), answering negatively a question of Esnault and Kerz [EK20, Question 9.1(1)].

items.name: Equivalence of finiteness, arithmeticity, geometric origin and integral variations
items.statement: With K and (C, x₁, …, x_n) as above and ρ : π₁^ét(C_{K̄} \ {x₁, …, x_n}) → GL_r(ℚ̄_ℓ) continuous with dim ρ < √(g+1), the following are equivalent: (1) ρ has finite image; (2) ρ is arithmetic; (3) for any embedding K ↪ ℂ and isomorphism ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ the corresponding complex local system is of geometric origin; (4) the same local system underlies an integral PVHS. Moreover (1), (3) and (4) are equivalent whenever dim ρ < 2√(g+1).
items.note: The equivalence of (1) and (2) is Theorem 9.1.2; (3) implies (4) because a local system of geometric origin underlies an integral PVHS; (4) implies (1) in the wider range by [LL22, Corollary 1.2.7], applied at an analytically very general complex point of M_{g,n}. Remark 9.1.5 explains that the relative Fontaine–Mazur conjecture predicts the bound of Theorem 9.1.2 should be improvable to 2√(g+1) for semisimple representations, while the bound of Theorem 8.5.3 cannot be, since arithmeticity is strictly stronger than MCG-finiteness.

items.name: Local systems of geometric origin
items.statement: A local system V on a smooth complex variety X is of geometric origin if there are a Zariski open U ⊂ X and a smooth proper morphism f : Y → U such that V|_U is a subquotient of R^i f_*ℂ for some i.
items.note: The notion the relative Fontaine–Mazur conjecture and Simpson's motivicity conjecture are about; it is also what Question 10.1.5 asks for local systems on M_{g,n}.

items.name: Residual representations of geometric origin
items.statement: Let K be an algebraically closed field, X/K a variety, 𝔽 a finite field of characteristic different from that of K and L the fraction field of the Witt vectors W(𝔽). A continuous representation ρ : π₁^ét(X_K) → GL_r(𝔽) is of geometric origin if there is a continuous representation ξ : π₁^ét(X_K) → GL_r(L) admitting a ξ-stable O_L-lattice W ⊂ L^r with W ⊗ 𝔽 ≅ ρ ⊗ 𝔽 and a dense open U ⊂ X with a smooth proper morphism π : Y → U such that ξ|_{π₁^ét(U_K)} is a subquotient of the monodromy representation of R^iπ_*L for some i.
items.note: That is, a residual representation is of geometric origin when it is the reduction of a characteristic-zero representation of geometric origin. This is the notion in which the paper produces, to its knowledge, the first examples of residual representations of geometric fundamental groups that are not of geometric origin.

items.name: Residual representations of a generic curve without arithmetic lifts
items.statement: Let K and (C, x₁, …, x_n) be as in Theorem 9.1.2. Then for 1 < r < √(g+1) and p sufficiently large in terms of r, no surjective representation ρ : π₁^ét(C_{K̄} \ {x₁, …, x_n}) → GL_r(𝔽_p) admits an arithmetic lift to characteristic zero; in particular no such representation is of geometric origin.
items.note: An immediate consequence of Theorem 9.1.2: an arithmetic lift would have finite image, and a finite-image lift cannot reduce to a surjection onto GL_r(𝔽_p) once p is large. Remark 9.2.4 observes that this contradicts a particularly optimistic extension of de Jong's conjecture, proven by Gaitsgory, from curves over finite fields to curves over arbitrary finitely generated fields.

items.name: Existence of surjective residual representations of a punctured curve
items.statement: Fix g, n ≥ 0 with n ≥ 1 if g = 1 and n ≥ 3 if g = 0, and 1 < r < √(g+1). For any n-pointed genus g curve (C, x₁, …, x_n) and any p there exist surjective representations ρ : π₁^ét(C_{K̄} \ {x₁, …, x_n}) → GL_r(𝔽_p): if n > 0 the group is profinite free on at least two generators and GL_r(𝔽_p) is generated by two elements [Wat89]; if n = 0 and g ≥ 2 the group surjects onto a free profinite group on g generators.
items.note: Supplies the representations to which Corollary 9.2.2 applies, so that the non-liftable residual representations actually exist. The surjection onto a free profinite group on g generators is obtained from the standard presentation by sending a_i ↦ c_i and b_i ↦ id.

items.name: Deformation rings of residual representations of arithmetic fundamental groups need not be complete intersections
items.statement: Deformation rings of absolutely irreducible 𝔽_p-representations of the arithmetic fundamental group π₁^ét(C_{K̄} \ {x₁, …, x_n}) of a generic curve over a finitely generated field need not be complete intersections over ℤ_p, since by Example 9.2.3 they are not flat over ℤ_p; this is in contrast with the case of curves over finite fields, where de Jong's conjecture, proven by Gaitsgory, gives complete intersections.
items.note: This answers negatively, for arithmetic fundamental groups of generic smooth curves, the question of Flach [CO05, p. 7] whether deformation rings of absolutely irreducible residual representations of profinite groups are always complete intersections; the answer was already known to be no in general, see [EM16].

items.name: Finiteness for representations of finite-index subgroups of the mapping class group
items.statement: Let Γ ⊂ PMod_{g,n+1} be a finite-index subgroup containing the point-pushing subgroup and let ρ be a representation of Γ of rank < √(g+1) whose restriction to the point-pushing subgroup is irreducible and whose determinant is finite. Then ρ has finite image.
items.note: Follows from Theorem 1.2.1, Lemma 2.4.1(1) and Proposition 2.1.2. It is compared with [FLM01, Theorem 1.6], which shows there are no faithful linear representations of finite-index subgroups of Mod_{g,0} of dimension < 2√(g − 1); the two results are not comparable, but both bounds are asymptotic to √g.

items.name: Non-rigid reducible representations of mapping class groups
items.statement: Three constructions: (1) Morita's nonzero class σ ∈ H¹(Mod_g, (∧³H)/H) with H = H₁(Σ_g, ℚ), related to the Johnson homomorphism, yielding a non-split extension 1 → ∧³H/H → W → ℚ → 1 and hence a non-rigid representation ℚ ⊕ ∧³H/H; (2) for n > 0, the non-split extension 0 → I²/I³ → I/I³ → I/I² → 0 of PMod_{g,n}-representations coming from the augmentation ideal I ⊂ ℚ[π₁(Σ_{g,n−1}, x)]; (3) the non-torsion class in H¹(Mod_{g,1}, H¹(Σ_g, ℤ)) of [Mor89, Proposition 6.4], giving a non-split extension 1 → H¹(Σ_g, ℚ) → W → ℚ → 1 whose restriction to the point-pushing subgroup is the unipotent representation γ · e = e + a(γ) of rank 2g + 1.
items.note: These show that the analogy between mapping class groups and lattices in higher-rank simple Lie groups only goes so far, and construction (3) gives the non-trivial unipotent MCG-finite representation of π₁(Σ_g) of rank 2g + 1 that bounds how far Theorem 1.2.1 can be improved.

items.name: Sharpness of the rank bounds in low genus
items.statement: The bound of Theorem 1.2.1 is sharp for g = 1: there are semisimple two-dimensional special dihedral MCG-finite representations of π₁(Σ_{1,n}) for n > 0 with infinite image [BGMW17, Theorem B], and two-dimensional non-semisimple MCG-finite representations [CH19, Theorem B], which also show the bound in Lemma 8.6.1 is sharp. The bound is not sharp for g = 2 and g = 3, since by [CH19, Theorem B] and [BGMW17, Theorem A] there are no two-dimensional MCG-finite representations with infinite image in those genera.
items.note: The special dihedral representations of [BGMW17, Theorem B] are in general not arithmetic in the sense of Definition 9.1.1, because their local monodromy at infinity need not be quasi-unipotent; this is consistent with Remark 9.1.5.

items.name: A rank N + 1 representation of a free group with Out(F_N)-fixed conjugacy class
items.statement: A variant of Example 10.1.6(3) gives a representation of the free group F_N on N generators, of rank N + 1, whose conjugacy class is fixed by Out(F_N) [PR00, p. 1444]; for N = 2 it is generated by the two unipotent 3 × 3 matrices with a single off-diagonal entry in the first and second rows. Conjecturally (Conjecture 10.2.8) there exist, for all N, semisimple representations of F_N with infinite image whose conjugacy class has finite Out(F_N)-orbit.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Remark 10.2.7 and Conjecture 10.2.8, pp. 52–53
items.note: The example shows the bound of Corollary 1.6.1 cannot be improved much for non-semisimple representations. Conjecture 10.2.8 deliberately contradicts a conjecture of Grunewald and Lubotzky [GL09, §9.2] which, combined with [FH17], would imply that no such semisimple examples exist for N ≥ 3.

items.name: The Gauss–Manin composite is the adjoint derivative of the period map
items.statement: With dP' : F¹H → (H/F¹H) ⊗ T_B^∨ the adjoint of dP, one has ∇ = dP'.
items.note: The first step of the proof of Theorem 5.1.6, following [Voi07, §§9–10]: it identifies the differential-geometric derivative of the period map with the algebraic Gauss–Manin composite of (5.3).

items.name: Logarithmic Dolbeault complexes and the interior product
items.statement: Let A^{i,j}_{log D}(ℰ) be the sheaf of C^∞ logarithmic (i, j)-forms valued in the Deligne canonical extension ℰ and A^n_{log D}(ℰ) = ⊕_{i+j=n} A^{i,j}_{log D}(ℰ). Then (A^{i,•}_{log D}(ℰ), ∂̄) is the Dolbeault complex of ℰ ⊗ Ω^i_{C̄}(log D) and (A^•_{log D}(ℰ), ∇ + ∂̄) is the de Rham resolution of the unitary local system V, with relative variants A^{i,j}_{log D, C̄/B}(ℰ). For v a C^∞ vector field on an open U ⊂ C̄ tangent to D and w a C^∞ section of A^i_{log D}(ℰ), the interior product int(v)(w) is defined by int(v)(w)(X₁, …, X_{i+j−1}) = w(v, X₁, …, X_{i+j−1}).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Notations A.1.2 and A.1.3, pp. 54–55
items.note: The C^∞ machinery in which the computation of the derivative of the period map is carried out; tangency to D is what keeps everything logarithmic.

items.name: A C^∞ formula for the Gauss–Manin connection
items.statement: Let σ ∈ A¹_{log D}(ℰ) be a differential form such that σ|_{C̄_{b'}} is closed for each b' ∈ B, so that σ represents a section [σ] of H. Fix b ∈ B and u ∈ T_{B,b}, and let v be a C^∞ section of T_{C̄}|_{C̄_b} tangent to D with u = π_*(v). Then ∇_GM([σ])|_b(u) = [int(v)((∇ + ∂̄)(σ)|_{C̄_b})] ∈ H_b.
items.note: The concrete computation of the Gauss–Manin connection in the logarithmic de Rham resolution, which is what allows the derivative of the period map to be compared with a cup product.

items.name: The logarithmic Kodaira–Spencer map
items.statement: From the short exact sequence 0 → T_{C̄_b}(− log D) → T_{C̄}(− log D)|_{C̄_b} → π^*T_B|_{C̄_b} → 0, with T_{C̄}(− log D) the dual of Ω¹_{C̄}(log D), the Kodaira–Spencer map κ : T_{B,b} → H¹(T_{C̄_b}(− log D)) is the connecting homomorphism, sending a vector v ∈ T_{B,b} ≅ H⁰(C̄_b, π^*T_B|_{C̄_b}) to its image in H¹.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Definition A.1.5 and Remark A.1.6, p. 56, equation (A.1)
items.note: Geometrically, κ sends a deformation of the pointed curve (C̄_b, D_b) to the corresponding class in H¹(T_{C̄_b}(−D)); for D = ∅ the identification of the connecting map with this description is [Voi07, §9.1.2], and the case D ≠ ∅ is analogous. Serre duality identifies κ with the pullback c^*_b of Theorem 5.1.6.

items.name: The derivative of the period map as a cup product with the Kodaira–Spencer class
items.statement: With C = C̄_b, D = D_b and E = ℰ|_C, the map dP''_b adjoint to the derivative of the period map fits into a commuting square: H⁰(C, E ⊗ Ω¹_C(D)) ⊗ T_{B,b} → H¹(C, E) equals the composition of 1 ⊗ κ, the cup product into H¹(C, E ⊗ Ω¹_C(D) ⊗ T_C(−D)) and the map α induced by the pairing Ω¹_C(D) ⊗ T_C(−D) → O_C.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Proposition A.1.7, p. 56, diagram (A.2)
items.note: The classical shape of the derivative of a period map: cup product with the Kodaira–Spencer class, contracted by the natural pairing. Here the logarithmic twists keep track of the punctures.

items.name: Serre-duality compatibility of the cup product with the multiplication map
items.statement: Let E be a vector bundle on a smooth curve C and D ⊂ C a divisor. The map H¹(C, T_C(−D)) ⊗ H⁰(C, E ⊗ ω_C(D)) → H¹(C, E) induced by the Yoneda cup-product composition α ∘ ∪ is adjoint to a map υ : H⁰(C, E ⊗ ω_C(D)) ⊗ H¹(C, E)^∨ → H¹(C, T_C(−D))^∨, and the square relating υ to the multiplication map μ : H⁰(C, E ⊗ ω_C(D)) ⊗ H⁰(C, E^∨ ⊗ ω_C) → H⁰(C, ω_C^{⊗2}(D)) obtained from the trace pairing commutes, the vertical maps being induced by Serre duality.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Lemma A.1.8, p. 57, diagram (A.3)
items.note: The last step of the proof of Theorem 5.1.6: it converts the cup-product description of Proposition A.1.7 into the multiplication-of-global-sections description, and identifies the Kodaira–Spencer map with the Serre dual of the pullback along the classifying map.

items.name: Fundamental groups, covering spaces and the Galois correspondence
items.statement: The fundamental group of a pointed topological space, the theory of covering maps, the universal cover of a semilocally simply connected space and the Galois correspondence between subgroups of π₁ and connected covers, together with the long exact sequence of homotopy groups of a fibration.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), used throughout, e.g. Notation 1.10.3, p. 11, and Lemma 2.1.5, p. 13
items.note: Mathlib has the fundamental groupoid and the fundamental group, and covering maps; Tau Ceti adds basepoint change for the fundamental group and the covering-space theory of aspherical spaces. The roadmap layers tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/UniversalCovers stages 1 and 2 plan the universal cover and the Galois correspondence, and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology stage 5 plans bundles, covers and the Leray spectral sequence.

items.name: Free groups and their universal property
items.statement: The free group on a set, with its universal property and the description of its elements by reduced words.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Corollary 1.6.1, p. 5, and Remark 1.6.3, p. 6
items.note: Mathlib defines FreeGroup with the full lifting API. What is missing is the outer automorphism group and Nielsen's presentation of Aut(F_N), which is recorded as a separate item.

items.name: Outer automorphism groups and Nielsen's generators of the automorphism group of a free group
items.statement: For a group G, the outer automorphism group Out(G) = Aut(G)/Inn(G) with its action on conjugacy classes of representations, and Nielsen's generating set for Aut(F_N) consisting of the cyclic permutation, the transposition of the first two generators, the inversion of the first generator and the elementary Nielsen transformation (A₁, A₂, …) ↦ (A₁A₂, A₂, …).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Corollary 1.6.1 and Remarks 1.6.3, 10.2.9, pp. 5–6 and p. 53, quoting [Nie24] and [MKS04, Theorem 3.2, p. 131]
items.note: Neither library has the outer automorphism group as a named object, and a name search for Out or outerAutomorphism at the pinned commits returns nothing; Mathlib has MulAut and the inner automorphism map but not the quotient. No layer of the atlas plans it.

items.name: Schur's lemma, isotypic components and semisimple decompositions
items.statement: Schur's lemma for irreducible representations over an algebraically closed field, the isotypic decomposition of a semisimple module, and the fact that a representation with a semisimple restriction to a normal subgroup decomposes accordingly.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Lemma 2.2.2, p. 14; Notation 7.1.1, p. 35; Lemma 8.6.1, p. 44
items.note: Planned by the Tau Ceti roadmap on semisimple algebras, whose layer 1 is exactly simple modules, Schur and isotypic components, and by the character-theory roadmap's Wedderburn layer. Mathlib and Tau Ceti already have substantial parts of this (FDRep, Simple, IsSemisimpleModule), but the atlas layer is the right owner.
