items.name: The sum of the squares of the irreducible degrees is the order of the group
items.statement: For a finite group H, the sum over the irreducible complex characters of the squares of their degrees equals #H.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), used in Corollary 7.2.4, p. 36, quoted there as [FH91, (2.19)]
items.note: Tau Ceti proves this as an identity of natural numbers, indexing the irreducible characters by the conjugacy classes and reading the degrees off a Wedderburn presentation of the group algebra. Verified in TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/Table.lean at the pinned commit.

items.name: Unitary groups, averaging and unitarizability
items.statement: The unitary group of a Hermitian form, the equivalence between having compact closure and preserving a positive-definite Hermitian form, and Weyl's unitarian trick producing an invariant inner product by averaging over a compact group.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Notation 1.10.2, p. 11, and throughout §8
items.note: Mathlib has the matrix unitary group but not the averaging statement for a representation with relatively compact image. The Tau Ceti roadmap on compact groups plans normalized Haar measure and averaging in layer 0 and unitarizability in layer 1, which is the right owner for the equivalence the paper uses.

items.name: Group cohomology in low degrees and extensions of representations
items.statement: The cohomology of a group with coefficients in a module, with H¹ classifying crossed homomorphisms modulo principal ones, the identification Ext¹_G(ρ₂, ρ₁) = H¹(G, Hom(ρ₂, ρ₁)), and the inflation–restriction sequence relating H⁰(Q, H¹(N, −)) to H¹ of an extension.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Lemmas 3.1.1 and 3.1.2, pp. 21–22, and Lemma 8.6.1, p. 44
items.note: Mathlib has group cohomology with the low-degree API, including H1 and the classification of extensions. The specific statements the paper needs about deformations with constant determinant are separate items routed to the deformation-theory layers.

items.name: Riemann–Roch, Serre duality and the dualizing sheaf on a curve
items.statement: Divisors, line and vector bundles on a smooth proper curve, the dualizing sheaf ω_C, Riemann–Roch and Serre duality H^i(C, F)^∨ ≅ H^{1−i}(C, F^∨ ⊗ ω_C).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), §§5.1.5 and 5.2 and Appendix A, pp. 29–31 and 54–57
items.note: Planned by the foundational layer SF.3, which integrates the Tau Ceti roadmaps on algebraic curves and the Jacobian challenge, and by the Jacobian challenge layer B on coherent cohomology over a field. This is the ambient coherent-cohomology theory in which every statement of §5 and Appendix A is made.

items.name: Clifford's theorem and its vector-bundle analogues
items.statement: Clifford's bound on the number of global sections of a special divisor on a curve, and the analogous bounds for semistable vector bundles which underlie the parabolic estimate of Proposition 5.2.4.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), used through [LL22, §6] at Proposition 5.2.4, p. 31
items.note: Clifford's theorem for line bundles is planned by the Tau Ceti algebraic-curves layer 5 on consequences of Riemann–Roch. The vector-bundle and parabolic generalisations the paper actually uses are not planned anywhere and are part of the new material routed here.

items.name: Poincaré duality and the intersection pairing on a surface
items.statement: Poincaré duality for a closed oriented surface and the induced intersection pairing on H₁(Σ_{g'}, ℂ), which is equivariant for the mapping class group.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), used at p. 38 in the proof of Theorem 7.2.1
items.note: Planned by the Tau Ceti algebraic-topology roadmap, stage 6, which covers cohomology, cup and cap products and manifold duality. It is the step that transfers the statement for H¹(Σ_{g',n'}) to the statement for H₁(Σ_{g'}) in Theorem 7.2.1.

items.name: The Leray spectral sequence of a fibration
items.statement: The Leray spectral sequence H^p(M, R^qπ_*F) ⇒ H^{p+q}(C, F) for a map π : C → M and a sheaf F, in particular the five-term exact sequence relating H¹(C, F) to H¹(M, π_*F) and H⁰(M, R¹π_*F).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), used in Lemma 8.1.3, p. 39, and Proposition 8.2.1, pp. 39–40
items.note: Planned by the Tau Ceti algebraic-topology roadmap, stage 5, which covers bundles, covers and the Leray spectral sequence, and in the étale setting by the classical étale-cohomology layer H0. Every vanishing statement of §8 is obtained by feeding Theorem 6.2.1 into this spectral sequence.

items.name: Grassmannians and their tangent bundles
items.statement: The Grassmannian Gr(s, r) of s-dimensional subspaces of an r-dimensional vector space, its universal sub- and quotient bundles, and the identification of its tangent bundle with Hom of the universal sub into the universal quotient.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), §5.1.2 and §5.1.4, p. 28, quoting [EH16, Theorem 3.5]
items.note: Planned by the moduli roadmap's projective parameter spaces layer R09.1 and by the Hilbert and Quot functor layer R09.2. The period map takes values in a Grassmannian because the Hodge filtration here has only two steps.

items.name: The moduli stack of n-pointed genus g curves and its Deligne–Mumford compactification
items.statement: The moduli stack M_{g,n} of smooth proper n-pointed genus g curves with geometrically connected fibres is a smooth separated Deligne–Mumford stack of dimension 3g − 3 + n, with a Deligne–Mumford compactification M̄_{g,n} by stable pointed curves whose boundary is a normal crossings divisor, and it admits finite étale covers that are schemes.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Notation 1.10.1, p. 10, and p. 40, using [PdJ95, Proposition 2.3.4]
items.note: The atlas plans algebraic stacks and moduli-stack algebraicity in layer R09.4 and coarse spaces in R09.5, but the stated targets there are generalised elliptic curves and polarised abelian schemes; M_{g,n} itself is not planned, and neither is M̄_{g,n}, although the Tau Ceti stable-reduction roadmap plans stable pointed curves and marked stabilisation.

items.name: Strict normal crossings compactification of the moduli stack and boundary monodromy
items.statement: A strict normal crossings compactification M̄'_{g,n+1} of M_{g,n+1} is obtained by blowing up boundary strata of the Deligne–Mumford compactification, which is only normal crossings; the local monodromy about its boundary components corresponds, under π₁(M_{g,n+1}) = PMod_{g,n+1}, to products of commuting Dehn twists about simple closed curves.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), p. 40, in the proof of Lemma 8.3.3, quoting [LLSS20, Lemma 2.1.1]
items.note: This is what makes the quasi-unipotence hypothesis of the integrality theorem checkable, via Proposition 8.3.2. The atlas plans characteristic-zero resolution and normal-crossings compactification in general at R09.7, but not this statement about the moduli of curves.

items.name: Galois categories, the étale fundamental group and its comparison with the topological one
items.statement: The étale fundamental group of a connected scheme as the automorphism group of a geometric fibre functor on finite étale covers, base-point change, and, over ℂ, the comparison with the profinite completion of the topological fundamental group.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), Definition 9.1.1 and §9.1, pp. 45–47, quoting [GR71, Exposé XII, Corollaire 5.2]
items.note: Planned by the inverse-Galois roadmap: IG.0 constructs Galois categories and fibre functors and IG.1 the arithmetic exact sequences and specialisation. The paper's own statements about the outer Galois action on π₁^ét of a curve over a finitely generated field are recorded as separate items.

items.name: Profinite groups, profinite completion and residual finiteness
items.statement: Profinite groups and profinite completion of a discrete group, with the density of a residually finite group in its profinite completion.
items.note: Planned by the Tau Ceti roadmap on profinite and pro-p groups, layer 0 on profinite foundations. The specific exactness statement for profinite completions of extensions with centreless kernel, and the residual finiteness of surface groups, are recorded as items of their own.

items.name: Lafforgue's correspondence and Deligne's companions over function fields
items.statement: The Langlands correspondence for GL_n over a global function field, matching cuspidal automorphic representations with finite-order central character and irreducible continuous n-dimensional ℓ-adic representations with finite-order determinant, and the resulting cases of Deligne's companion conjectures.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.15352v4 (23 February 2025), used through [EG18] and [KP20b] at p. 40
items.note: Planned by the global shtuka roadmap, layer GS.6, which develops Lafforgue's independent GL_n route and states the bijection with its conventions, building on the weights layer DWP.7. This is the deepest external input to the paper, entering through the integrality theorem for cohomologically rigid local systems.

items.name: Deformation functors of representations and their representability
items.statement: Deformation functors of a residual or complex representation on Artin local rings, their tangent spaces, representability and universal deformation rings.
items.note: Planned by the global Galois deformation roadmap, layers R04.1 and R04.2. The paper's §3 works with representations of abstract groups rather than Galois groups, and its §9.2 produces a counterexample to a complete-intersection expectation for such rings; both are routed to those layers.

prerequisites.citation: Aaron Landesman and Daniel Litt, Geometric local systems on very general curves and isomonodromy, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), 683–729
prerequisites.why: The authors' companion paper, quoted as [LL22]. It supplies Theorem 1.2.12 (a complex variation of Hodge structure of rank less than 2√(g+1) on a very general curve is unitary), Corollary 1.2.7 (an integral variation of that rank has finite monodromy), Lemma 7.2.1 (a representation into GL_r(O_K) unitary at every embedding has finite image) and the parabolic estimate Proposition 6.3.6. It is the single most heavily used input and is not covered anywhere in the atlas.

prerequisites.citation: V. B. Mehta and C. S. Seshadri, Moduli of vector bundles on curves with parabolic structures, Math. Ann. 248 (1980), 205–239
prerequisites.why: The correspondence between parabolically stable parabolic bundles of parabolic degree zero on (C, D) and irreducible unitary local systems on C \ D, which is what turns the analytic period-map computation into a statement about vector bundles.

prerequisites.citation: Takuro Mochizuki, Kobayashi–Hitchin correspondence for tame harmonic bundles and an application, Astérisque 309 (2006)
prerequisites.why: Non-abelian Hodge theory for quasi-projective varieties: Theorem 10.5 deforms any representation with finite determinant to one underlying a complex variation of Hodge structure, and Lemma 10.13 does this G-equivariantly. Simpson's projective case [Sim92] and his work on noncompact curves [Sim90] belong with it.

prerequisites.citation: Hélène Esnault and Michael Groechenig, Cohomologically rigid local systems and integrality, Selecta Math. (N.S.) 24 (2018), 4279–4292
prerequisites.why: The first integrality theorem for cohomologically rigid local systems, and the source of the identification H¹(X̄, j_{!*} ad ρ) ≅ H¹(U, a_* ad ρ) used in Lemma 8.1.3.

prerequisites.citation: Christian Klevdal and Stefan Patrikis, G-rigid local systems are integral, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 374 (2021), 6117–6148
prerequisites.why: Theorem 1.2 there is the integrality statement the paper applies to the PGL_r-local system attached to ρ̃; it is the conduit through which the Langlands correspondence over function fields and the companion conjectures enter the proof.

prerequisites.citation: Andrew Putman and Ben Wieland, Abelian quotients of subgroups of the mapping class group and higher Prym representations, J. Lond. Math. Soc. (2) 88 (2013), 79–96
prerequisites.why: Conjecture 1.2 there is the Putman–Wieland conjecture, restated as Conjecture 7.1.3 and proved here for small groups; the paper also takes the term higher Prym representation from it.

prerequisites.citation: Joseph Steenbrink and Steven Zucker, Variation of mixed Hodge structure I, Invent. Math. 80 (1985), 489–542; Chris Peters and Joseph Steenbrink, Mixed Hodge Structures, Ergebnisse 52, Springer, 2008
prerequisites.why: The definitions of variation of mixed Hodge structure, graded-polarizability and admissibility, and the theorem of the fixed part in the form quoted as Theorem 4.2.1.

prerequisites.citation: Morihiko Saito, Mixed Hodge modules, Publ. Res. Inst. Math. Sci. 26 (1990), 221–333; Christian Schnell, An overview of Morihiko Saito's theory of mixed Hodge modules
prerequisites.why: Used to prove graded-polarizability and admissibility in Theorem 4.1.1: Rj_*V_ℝ underlies an object of the derived category of real mixed Hodge modules, and [Sch19, Theorem 21.1] converts local constancy into an admissible variation.

prerequisites.citation: Klaus Timmerscheidt, Mixed Hodge theory for unitary local systems, J. reine angew. Math. 379 (1987), 152–171
prerequisites.why: The pointwise mixed Hodge structure on the cohomology of a unitary local system on a punctured curve, its weight filtration, and the degeneration of the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence that gives the two-step Hodge filtration.

prerequisites.citation: Pierre Deligne, Équations différentielles à points singuliers réguliers, Lecture Notes in Math. 163, Springer, 1970
prerequisites.why: The canonical extension of a flat bundle with regular singularities, its logarithmic de Rham complex, and the hypercohomology comparison used throughout §5.

prerequisites.citation: Gaël Cousin and Viktoria Heu, Algebraic isomonodromic deformations and the mapping class group, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 20 (2021), 1497–1545
prerequisites.why: Theorem A there is the dictionary between algebraic universal isomonodromic deformations and finite mapping class group orbits which converts Theorem 1.2.1 into Corollary 1.2.3; Theorem B classifies the rank-two non-semisimple case and gives the sharpness examples of Remarks 10.2.1 and 10.2.2.

prerequisites.citation: Stefan Wewers, Construction of Hurwitz spaces, Thesis, Universität Essen, 1998
prerequisites.why: Theorem 4 there constructs the versal family of ϕ-covers of Definition 7.3.1, as a Deligne–Mumford stack whose points have isotropy the centre of H; the whole proof of Theorem 7.2.1 is run over such a family.

prerequisites.citation: Benson Farb and Dan Margalit, A Primer on Mapping Class Groups, Princeton Math. Ser. 49, Princeton Univ. Press, 2012
prerequisites.why: The standard reference for the mapping class group: the Birman exact sequence (p. 98), the contractibility of Teichmüller space and the identification π₁(M_{g,n}) ≅ PMod_{g,n} (§10.6.3 and p. 353), generating sets, and the structure of the kernel of PMod_{g,b,p} → PMod_{g,0,b+p} (Theorem 3.18).

prerequisites.citation: Javier Aramayona and Juan Souto, Rigidity phenomena in the mapping class group, Handbook of Teichmüller theory VI, 2016, 131–165
prerequisites.why: Proposition 2.4 there says that in any linear representation of a finite-index subgroup of Mod_{g,n} with g ≥ 3 a power of a Dehn twist acts quasi-unipotently; this is what lets the quasi-unipotence hypothesis of the integrality theorem be checked.

prerequisites.citation: Wanlin Li, Daniel Litt, Nick Salter and Padmavathi Srinivasan, Surface bundles and the section conjecture, Math. Ann. 386 (2023), 1–54
prerequisites.why: Lemma 2.1.1 there identifies the local monodromy about boundary components of a strict normal crossings compactification of M_{g,n+1} with products of commuting Dehn twists, which is the other half of the quasi-unipotence verification in Lemma 8.3.3.

prerequisites.citation: Claire Voisin, Hodge Theory and Complex Algebraic Geometry I and II, Cambridge Stud. Adv. Math. 76 and 77, 2007
prerequisites.why: The model computation of the derivative of a period map, Lemmas 10.19 and 10.22 and Theorem 10.21, which Appendix A follows and generalises to unitary coefficients on a punctured curve; also the description of the Kodaira–Spencer map as a connecting homomorphism (§9.1.2).

prerequisites.citation: Adam S. Sikora, Character varieties, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 364 (2012), 5173–5208
prerequisites.why: Theorem 30 there says the conjugation orbit of a semisimple representation is closed in the representation variety, which is what lets Lemma 8.5.2 propagate a statement from a dense open subset of the base to the whole base.

routes.title: Mapping class groups and canonical representations of surface groups
routes.brief: Plan the theory of mapping class groups of surfaces and of the canonical — that is, mapping-class-group-finite — representations of surface groups, following Landesman and Litt, Annals of Mathematics 199 (2024), no. 2, together with the topological background it assumes. The final theorems are these. (1) Main theorem (Theorem 1.2.1): if ρ : π₁(Σ_{g,n}) → GL_r(ℂ) is MCG-finite, meaning its conjugacy class has finite orbit under Mod_{g,n}, and r < √(g+1), then ρ has finite image; equivalently (Corollary 1.6.1) a representation of a free group F_N of rank r < √(g+1), N = 2g or 2g+1, whose conjugacy class has finite Out(F_N)-orbit has finite image. (2) The Putman–Wieland theorem (Theorem 7.2.1): for ϕ : π₁(Σ_{g,b,p}) ↠ H with cover Σ_{g',b',p'} and Γ the stabiliser of ϕ in PMod_{g,b,p+1}, the ρ-isotypic component of H¹(Σ_{g',b',p'}, ℂ) has no nonzero Γ'-invariant subrepresentation of dimension less than 2g − 2 dim ρ, for any finite-index Γ' ⊆ Γ and any irreducible H-representation ρ; hence the Putman–Wieland conjecture holds for every H with #H < g². (3) The arithmetic theorem (Theorem 9.1.2): on a curve whose moduli point is the generic point of M_{g,n,ℚ̄}, every continuous arithmetic representation of the geometric étale fundamental group of rank r < √(g+1) has finite image, with the four-way equivalence of Corollary 9.1.4 and the non-liftable residual representations of Corollary 9.2.2. Cover, in layers: the surface Σ_{g,n}, its fundamental group and standard presentation, Dehn twists, Mod_{g,n} and PMod_{g,n} with a generating set, and the Birman exact sequence with its point-pushing subgroup; the identification π₁(M_{g,n}) ≅ PMod_{g,n} coming from the contractibility of Teichmüller space, and the compatibility of the outer actions; families of n-pointed curves, versal and punctured versal families, and the homotopy exact sequence 1 → π₁(C°) → π₁(C°) → π₁(M) → 1; MCG-finite representations with their closure properties, the finiteness of the determinant, and the two-way dictionary with representations of finite-index subgroups of Mod_{g,n+1} restricted to the point-pushing subgroup; the projective representation ρ̃ attached to an irreducible MCG-finite representation and its lifting to GL_r after a dominant étale base change, including the device that kills a finite abelian obstruction class; higher Prym representations, isotypic components, the Putman–Wieland property and versal families of ϕ-covers; then the three steps of the main proof — the unitary case, the semisimple case and the non-semisimple case — and finally §9's arithmetic consequences and §10's examples, in particular Morita's non-split extensions and the rank 2g+1 unipotent MCG-finite representation that bounds how far the theorem can be improved. Every definition gets its API and unit tests, and the open questions of §10 (rigidity of representations of finite-index subgroups of Mod_{g,n}, the minimal rank of an MCG-finite representation with infinite image, Conjecture 10.2.8 for free groups) are recorded as targets, not as theorems. Import, never re-plan: covering-space theory, the fundamental group and the Galois correspondence from the Tau Ceti roadmaps UniversalCovers and AlgebraicTopology, together with Poincaré duality and the Leray spectral sequence from AlgebraicTopology; finite-group representation theory, Schur's lemma and isotypic components from the Tau Ceti roadmaps SemisimpleAlgebras and CharacterTheory, including that the sum of the squares of the irreducible degrees is the order of the group; the moduli stack M_{g,n} and its Deligne–Mumford and strict-normal-crossings compactifications from AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.4, R09.5 and R09.7, which this extraction routes there; the étale fundamental group, the arithmetic exact sequence and the outer Galois action from InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.0 and IG.1; deformation functors from GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1; and the whole Hodge-theoretic engine — variations of mixed Hodge structure, the theorem of the fixed part, the period map on the cohomology of a unitary local system and its derivative, parabolic bundles and Mehta–Seshadri, cohomological rigidity and the integrality theorem, and the cohomological vanishing results Theorem 1.7.1 and Theorem 6.2.1 — from the Part II of the Tau Ceti Hodge-structures roadmap proposed alongside this route.
routes.reason: Nothing in the atlas goes in this direction. Its 211 roadmaps contain no mapping class group, no Teichmüller theory, no moduli of curves M_{g,n} as a topological object, and no character varieties of surface groups: a text search of every stage description at the pinned atlas for 'mapping class', 'Teichmüller', 'character variety' and 'Putman' returns only the Heegaard-splitting use of surface mapping classes in the Tau Ceti geometric-topology roadmap and unrelated hits. The Tau Ceti roadmap on Fuchsian groups and orbifold Riemann surfaces stops at the compactified quotient and the level-one modular quotient and never reaches the moduli of curves or its fundamental group; AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry plans stacks for generalised elliptic curves and polarised abelian schemes; InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups plans Hurwitz spaces with braid and Nielsen classes but not the mapping class group itself. A source route was therefore impossible, and a Part II would have had no parent: the material is a coherent new subject with its own targets — the classification of canonical representations of surface and free groups, the Putman–Wieland conjecture, Ivanov's conjecture, and the arithmetic of the generic curve — and its own literature.

routes.title: Hodge structures (pure, mixed, and polarized), Part II: variations, period maps and non-abelian Hodge theory
routes.brief: Extend the Tau Ceti roadmap Hodge structures (pure, mixed, and polarized) from linear algebra to geometry: variations of Hodge structure, period maps and non-abelian Hodge theory, as used by Landesman and Litt, Annals of Mathematics 199 (2024), no. 2, §§4–6 and 8 and Appendix A. It starts where the parent stops: that roadmap plans pure and mixed Hodge structures, polarizations and the points of a period domain, and states explicitly at milestone L3 that the manifold structure of the period domain belongs to a successor. The final theorems are these. (1) The variation of mixed Hodge structure on the cohomology of a unitary local system (Theorem 4.1.1): for a family of punctured curves π° : C° → M and V unitary with a real structure, R¹π°_*V_ℝ is an admissible graded-polarizable real variation of mixed Hodge structure with weights in [1,2], weight filtration R¹π_*j_*V_ℝ ⊂ R¹π°_*V_ℝ, and Hodge filtration induced by the filtration bête of the logarithmic relative de Rham complex of the Deligne canonical extension. (2) The derivative of the period map (Theorem 5.1.6): dP_b^∨ is the tensor product of global sections followed by the trace pairing E ⊗ E^∨ → O_C and the pullback along the classifying map to M_{g,n}. (3) The rank bound (Theorem 1.7.1): for a punctured versal family and V unitary, every nonzero sub-local system of R¹π°_*V has rank at least 2g − 2 rk V; and its Artinian consequence (Theorem 6.2.1): H⁰(M, R¹π°_*V) = 0 whenever V restricts on a fibre to a constant deformation of a unitary local system of rank less than g. (4) The rigidity and integrality package: cohomological and strong cohomological rigidity, the implication H¹(X, ad ρ) = 0 ⇒ cohomological rigidity, Proposition 8.2.1 producing rigidity for low-rank local systems with irreducible unitary fibres, and the theorem of Esnault–Groechenig and Klevdal–Patrikis that a cohomologically rigid local system with quasi-unipotent local monodromy is integral. Cover, in layers: complex polarizable variations of Hodge structure and variations of mixed Hodge structure with graded-polarizability and admissibility; the Deligne canonical extension of a flat bundle with regular singularities and its logarithmic de Rham complex; the theorem of the fixed part and the variant for irreducible local systems, with the real-form device L̃; Mochizuki's deformation theorem and the fact that cohomologically rigid semisimple representations with finite determinant underlie complex variations; the period map to a Grassmannian for a two-step Hodge filtration, its derivative, the Gauss–Manin composite ∇, and the full computation of Appendix A through logarithmic Dolbeault complexes, the logarithmic Kodaira–Spencer map and Serre duality; parabolic bundles with their weights, parabolic degree, slope and semistability, the Mehta–Seshadri correspondence with irreducible unitary local systems, the bilinear pairing B_E and the rank estimate Proposition 5.2.3 together with the parabolic Clifford-type bound it rests on; and the notion of a local system of geometric origin. Every definition gets its API and unit tests, and the results quoted from Mochizuki, Mehta–Seshadri, Simpson, Steenbrink–Zucker, Saito, Timmerscheidt, Esnault–Groechenig, Klevdal–Patrikis and the authors' own earlier work are recorded with their hypotheses and not re-proved. Import, never re-plan: pure, mixed and polarized Hodge structures and period-domain points from the parent roadmap's milestones L0 to L3; Riemann–Roch, Serre duality and the dualizing sheaf on a curve from SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.3 and the Tau Ceti Jacobian-challenge roadmap; Clifford's theorem from the Tau Ceti algebraic-curves roadmap, layer 5; Grassmannians and their tangent bundles from AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.1 and R09.2; the Leray spectral sequence from the Tau Ceti algebraic-topology roadmap, stage 5; Lafforgue's correspondence and Deligne's companions, which the integrality theorem rests on, from GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.6 and DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.7; and mapping class groups, moduli of curves and versal families from the new roadmap proposed alongside this route, Mapping class groups and canonical representations of surface groups, which is this roadmap's principal consumer.
routes.reason: The Tau Ceti roadmap Hodge structures plans pure Hodge structures and the Hodge decomposition (L0), polarization and Hodge–Riemann (L1), mixed Hodge structures and strictness (L2), and the points of a period domain with its symmetry group (L3); its L3 milestone says in so many words that the period domain's manifold structure is the successor roadmap, not that milestone. Everything this paper needs on the Hodge side is exactly that successor: variations of pure and mixed Hodge structure with graded-polarizability and admissibility, the theorem of the fixed part, the period map and its derivative, the Deligne canonical extension, and the non-abelian Hodge theory of Simpson–Mochizuki with the parabolic-bundle correspondence of Mehta–Seshadri that makes unitary local systems computable. A Tau Ceti roadmap is never re-planned, so this is routed as its Part II rather than as a source. A new roadmap was rejected because every layer is a direct continuation of L0–L3 and consumes them; a source route was rejected because none of these statements is planned by any existing layer — a search of every stage description for 'non-abelian Hodge', 'Higgs', 'parabolic bundle', 'variation of Hodge' and 'Simpson' at the pinned atlas returns nothing. The cohomological vanishing theorems 1.7.1 and 6.2.1 and the rigidity and integrality package are kept here rather than with the mapping class groups because they are theorems about period maps and parabolic bundles whose statements happen to be made over a family of curves.

IG.0 constructs Galois categories, fibre functors and the étale fundamental group with base-point change, and IG.1 plans the arithmetic exact sequences and specialization. The three items routed here are exactly statements of that kind: the definition of an arithmetic representation as one whose conjugacy class has finite orbit under the outer action of Gal(K̄/K) on π₁^ét(X_K̄); the exactness of 1 → π₁^ét(C°_K̄) → π₁^ét(C°) → Gal(K̄/K) → 1 and of its analogue over the moduli stack, together with the compatibility of the two induced outer actions, which rests on the étale fundamental group being the profinite completion of the topological one and on profinite completion preserving exactness when the kernel is centreless; and the density of the topological fundamental group of a punctured Riemann surface in its profinite completion. None of these is special to this paper, all three are general facts about arithmetic fundamental groups of curves, and IG.1 is the layer that already promises arithmetic exact sequences. The paper's own finiteness theorems for arithmetic representations are not routed here: they belong with the main theorem they are deduced from.

R04.1 plans deformation functors and R04.2 their representability and universal deformation rings. The three lemmas of §3 are ordinary deformation theory of a representation of an abstract group — first-order deformations with constant determinant are classified by H¹(G, ad ρ), a deformation restricts constantly to a normal subgroup when H⁰(Q, H¹(N, ad)) vanishes, and a ℂ[[t]]-family with that vanishing at every finite level is conjugate to a constant family on the normal subgroup — and they are stated in that generality in the paper. They belong in the layer that owns deformation functors, not in a roadmap about surfaces, and planning them once there serves every consumer. Routed with them are the definition of a residual representation of geometric origin, which is about lifting a mod-p representation to characteristic zero, and the paper's negative answer, for arithmetic fundamental groups of generic curves, to the question of whether deformation rings of absolutely irreducible residual representations are complete intersections: that is a statement about the universal deformation ring, hence about R04.2, and the paper is a good source for it because it exhibits the failure of flatness over ℤ_p explicitly.

R09.4 plans algebraic stacks in the required class, with Deligne–Mumford, separated, proper and tame as distinct properties proved separately; R09.5 plans coarse spaces and rigidification; R09.7 plans characteristic-zero resolution and normal-crossings compactification. The two items routed here are the algebraicity of the moduli stack M_{g,n} of smooth n-pointed genus g curves, with its Deligne–Mumford compactification and the existence of finite étale covers that are schemes, and the construction of a strict normal crossings compactification of M_{g,n+1} by blowing up boundary strata of M̄_{g,n+1}, whose boundary monodromy is generated by products of commuting Dehn twists. The stated targets of R09.4 today are generalised elliptic curves and polarised abelian schemes, so M_{g,n} is not yet planned there, but it is precisely the same kind of statement and PROTOCOL.md section 15 asks that a general missing notion be planned once in the layer that owns it rather than duplicated. The topological facts about M_{g,n} — the contractibility of its universal cover and the identification of its fundamental group with the pure mapping class group — stay with the new roadmap.
